Sports.title: Fraudster who pawned Edgar Davids’s £188,000 art collection misses sentencing after ‘being knocked out by luggage’
Sports.content:
NO SHOW Fraudster who pawned Edgar Davids’s £188,000 art collection misses sentencing after ‘being knocked out by luggage’

A FRAUDSTER who pawned Edgar Davids’ £188,000 art collection has claimed she failed to appear in court because she was knocked out by luggage.

The football legend, 52, allowed friend Nabila Habiby to stay at his Hadley Wood mansion in 2014.



Davids believed that Habiby was looking after his possessions while he moved into a new Central London flat in December of that year.

But a court has since heard that Habiby, 39, stole 37 pieces of art across the following two years before taking them to pawn brokers, with Davids believing that they were being stored at a unit in Enfield.



Habiby managed to obtain £31,500 in loans by handing over the 37 painting and works of art belonging to Davids.

The former Spurs and Ajax midfielder only realised his paintings had gone when Habiby defaulted on the loans.



A court heard that the pawn shops sold the art to collectors around the world with one getting in touch with him to inquire about the history of a painting.

Habiby pleaded guilty in September 2025 to two counts of fraud, and she was set free on bail with a warning that she could face up to 34 months in prison.

She has still not been sentenced, with the first attempt derailing after she made a failed attempt to withdraw her guilty pleas.

Her case was listed for sentence again today, but Habiby was absent from the dock at Wood Green Crown Court.



Defence barrister Hannah Thomas said: “I received correspondence this morning, at around 9.30am, saying on her way to the airport to come here she had been hit on the head by a piece of luggage en route.

“She had a concussion, since she passed out, and was taken to the hospital where she remains on a drip.”

Judge Emma Deacon KC said she had been handed “inadequate” medical evidence from Belgium – where Habiby now lives – to support her story, however.

The judge did agree to adjourn the sentencing hearing though, so that the original judge who oversaw the case when guilty pleas were entered could pass sentence.

It is now almost five years since Habiby was first charged after a Metropolitan Police investigation.



Her fraud offences date back to 2015 and 2016.

The court heard the former baller handed Habiby, a wealth manager, the keys to his home in Hadley Wood, Hertfordshire, when he was moving to an apartment in central London in December 2014.

She took his collection of works by artists Paul Insect and Ron English, which he had bought from the Opera Gallery in New York between 2006 and 2012, to pawnbrokers.

Some of the paintings have since been recovered, but 25 works of art are gone.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Habiby has been ordered to come to court on September 23 to be sentenced.



She has also been told to provide a full medical report to back up her absence from court on Friday.

Sports.title: Troy Parrott comes back to haunt Jose Mourinho as ex-Tottenham star comes off bench to score winner vs Real Madrid
Sports.content:
TROY PARROTT came back to haunt Jose Mourinho as he condemned him to his first defeat as Real Madrid manager.

The Ireland ace came off the bench to score an 81st-minute winner for Real Betis against the Spanish giants.

Mourinho had overseen a 100 per cent winning start to the season as Madrid kept pace with hated rivals Barcelona.



However, the first slip-up of the campaign came on Friday night against Betis as Parrott was quickest to react to a loose ball following a Thibaut Courtois save at a corner, and smashed home the winner into the roof of the net.



But Mourinho, 63, might have guessed such an event might happen given he handed Parrott his debut when he was manager of Tottenham.

Mourinho famously gave Parrott the match ball after his Premier League debut off the bench, a 5-0 win for Tottenham in 2019.

A missed Kylian Mbappe penalty then added salt to the wounds for an awful evening for Los Blancos, as Parrott became only the second Irishman to score against Real Madrid after John Aldridge’s goals for Real Sociedad in 1989-90 and 1990-91.

On the winning goal, Parrott – in comments which would certainly please compatriot Roy Keane – told ESPN: “That’s a striker’s job, to go in after the ball and hope it will fall in front of me.

“In a game I might do this 10 times and it might not happen.

“So it’s a mentality thing to just keep going in there and hopefully it comes, and today it did.”

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK



Parrott would go on to have loans at Millwall, Ipswich, MK Dons, Preston North End and Excelsior before leaving Spurs permanently in 2024.

He joined Dutch side AZ, scoring 51 goals in 97 games before signing for Betis in a £17.1million (€20m) deal this summer.

Parrott’s match-winning goal, on his home debut no less, moved Betis level with Madrid on points and into the top three of La Liga before the rest of the league play their games this weekend.

Mourinho had a few sour grapes about the result, however, saying: “Sometimes you lose and you don’t know why, and sometimes you lose and you don’t know how to explain it.



“We were in control for the most part, our defenders were fantastic and dominated everything, we did a lot of attacking work and created many scoring chances.

“If the match had ended in a draw, we would have left feeling frustrated because we did more, so imagine how we feel after the loss.

“I don’t know why we lost, and I can’t justify it, because the team played very well in all aspects.”

He sarcastically added: “I congratulate Real Betis, they played for the draw and came away with the big prize.”

Sports.title: Mason Greenwood and Matteo Guendouzi both BANNED and fined by Uefa for ‘offensive gestures’ aimed at rival fans
Sports.content:
MASON GREENWOOD and Matteo Guendouzi have both been hit by bans and fines from Uefa.

It comes after the Fenerbahce pair were involved in a heated exchange and then brawl on the pitch following the club’s 3-2 aggregate win over Lyon in the Champions League play-offs last month.



The duo both played for Lyon’s rivals Marseille in Ligue 1, but ex-Arsenal star Guendouzi was seen sticking his finger up and shouting “Allez l’OM” (“Go Marseille”) towards Lyon fans.

That saw the midfielder confronted by a man in Lyon colours as a mass brawl, which involved ex-Manchester United star Greenwood, erupted on the pitch.



This was followed by a brawl between both sides in the tunnel.

A Uefa investigation into the incident has now seen fit to slap the pair with punishment.

Guendouzi, 27, was punished for “insulting others present at the match, provoking spectators and for violating the basic rules of decent conduct”.

He has been slapped with a four-game ban in Europe, two of which are suspended “subject to a probationary period of one year”, and a fine of £43,000 (€50,000).

Meanwhile, Greenwood, 24, was given a one-match suspended ban for “violating the basic rules of decent conduct” over the same length of time as his team-mate and fined £26,000 (€30,000).

Speaking after the game, in which he was repeatedly booed by Lyon fans, Guendouzi said he felt “disrespected” by fans who were taunting him with “insults” about his family.

Sports.title: I was in awe of Morgan Rogers aged FOUR & watched him terrorise 13 year olds aged six… £117m Chelsea star is special
Sports.content:
MORGAN ROGERS has been terrorising defenders since he was FOUR.

The man who first spotted the talent of Chelsea’s £117million signing is adamant that the England international stood out from very young.



And on Sunday Rogers heads to Arsenal — who also wanted to sign him this summer — hoping to continue the Blues’ 100 per cent start to this season.

The Gunners were unwilling to go much above the £80m they offered Aston Villa for the attacker and it could come back to haunt them at the Emirates.



Rogers, 24, started his amazing journey in his home town of Halesowen in the West Midlands.

Birmingham cult hero Paul Tait organises soccer schools in the south of the city and remembers the day Rogers first crossed his path.

He said: “I ran — and still run — a Saturday morning coaching course for kids in Halesowen. Morgan’s parents brought him in when he was four.

“From the outset, he was a different level to everyone else. Even at that age. His dribbling. Awareness. Speed. He could kick with both feet. His movement. I was in awe of him.”

Tait, a teen prodigy for Birmingham back in the day, moved Rogers up the groups until he was embarrassing the ten to 13-year-old section at about six.

And Tait, 55, had links with the late, respected talent spotter Steve Hopcroft, who worked at Birmingham before moving to West Brom and then Villa.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Tait said: “I used to really like the Albion set-up back then. I formed a link with them through Steve — who sadly passed away a few months ago — and Mark Harrison, who was then the Baggies’ academy manager.

“Any player I thought would warrant further development, I took them there. Morgan went and after one session Hoppy rang and said, ‘We want him’.”

Rogers was playing for local team Halas Hawks by this stage and had to sacrifice Saturday mornings with Tait.

Tait said: “I just asked the kids to go out there and express themselves. I think that’s how he thrived. He’s gone on record saying he could do anything he wanted and enjoyed it.

“When players join academy set-ups, they mould them into what they want — into robots, a lot of them. I just give them the opportunity to be free and play with a smile on their face, which is what he did.”



Rogers moved from the Baggies to Manchester City’s academy before Middlesbrough signed him in July 2023.

When he was snapped up by Villa in the 2024 winter window for an initial £8m, there were some internal doubts before manager Unai Emery pressed the green light.

Tait revealed: “I spoke to Hopcroft about Morgan nine months or so before Villa signed him.

“They weren’t too enamoured with him at this stage. They thought he’d ‘dropped off a bit’. They’d watched him and were umming and ahing. The next thing you know, they went and bought him.

“It shows what can happen in football. It’s about maybe having that bit of luck — or a manager who has faith in you.”



And then some. Rogers was Emery’s go-to guy within days of him arriving at Villa Park from Teesside.

A trademark of Emery’s sides is the use of a free spirit — someone allowed to pop up anywhere along the frontline.

That took Rogers back to his roots, and led to Villa banking a whopping profit on the player, even with Boro cashing in on a hefty sell-on clause.



Tait added: “To get the best out of him, you have got to let him do what he was doing at Villa.

“He can find space. He’s intelligent. He knows where to go on a pitch. You don’t want to turn him into a regimented player. Xabi Alonso is a top manager and I’m sure he won’t.

“His work ethic is very good. He’s not one-dimensional. He is a big, strong boy, 6ft 3in. He doesn’t get pushed off the ball.

“With Cole Palmer — who has something to prove after not going to the World Cup — they will work well together. But as for Chelsea, I am not sure. I don’t know what to expect of them.

“Gone are those days when you knew what you were getting and who would start. The Terrys, Lampards, Drogbas.



“They now have that many players, you can’t keep track, and loads of youngsters who are loaned out. It’s a massive business, Chelsea.

“So, it does worry me a bit for Morgan and how it’s going to pan out. What is their identity? But I have every confidence in his ability.

“It’s been some journey for him and I truly hope he goes on to smash it at Stamford Bridge. It’s amazing to think back to all those years ago, when he was a little lad running around in mud in Halesowen having fun.



“Then winning the Europa League with Villa, playing for England, starring for Chelsea and costing £117m.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Did I think that he’d go on to do all that? No, of course not. But his talent shone through like a beacon.

“So, no one could have predicted it. But did I think it was possible? One hundred per cent — yes.”

Sports.title: Eagle-eyed fans convinced Man Utd match uncovered as one of Mike Dean’s controversial Premier League ‘mini-games’

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola 'never doubted' Cody Gakpo despite nearly completing Liverpool exit
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola 'never doubted' Cody Gakpo despite nearly completing Liverpool exit

Cody Gakpo played a starring role, creating both of Alexander Isak's goals, as Liverpool recorded their first Premier League win of the Andoni Iraola era

View 2 Images Cody Gakpo celebrates with Alexander Isak during Liverpool's win over Ipswich

Andoni Iraola insists he never doubted Cody Gakpo even after the Liverpool forward nearly quit Anfield.

‌



Gakpo could have left in the final days of the transfer window after Manchester City launched a bid to sign him but Liverpool blocked the move after failing to find replacements.

‌



Holland international Gakpo provided both assists for two-goal Alexander Isak in what was Liverpool’s first win under Iraola.

‌



Liverpool boss Iraola said: “Cody knows how much we value him. There is no doubt. I rate him very highly. There might be, obviously, strong competition for minutes because we have good players there in those positions.

“It's a matter of pushing each other. With Bradley Barcola, with Rio Ngumoha, with Victor Munoz, it's a matter of sometimes they will start, sometimes they will come from the bench, sometimes they will not play, but this is competition.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

“Cody has been very good all preseason. He started the season very well, producing numbers today. Then after the two assists, he finishes as number nine to help us close the game.

“I think it's good to have Cody because he can play in three positions up top, like other of our players. To have him in this place for this particular position is good.”

‌



Iraola was also full of praise for Isak who has now got three goals this season which is as many as he got for Liverpool in the entire Premier League campaign last year. Bradley Barcola also got his debut as a substitute after his £106m move.

It also marked Iraola’s first win as Liverpool manager and he admitted he was relieved to get it after two draws in their opening fixtures.

Iraola added: “If he's fit, if he's available, if he's in a good shape, I think he will produce the numbers. My demand with Alex will not be about the goals. Probably, it will be about other things.

‌



View 2 Images Gakpo played a starring role in the win over Ipswich

“I will demand other things so we can play well. And if we play well, we are in good positions. The goals will come. I think he has to contribute to the collective. And when everyone helps, I think the goals and the result will come.

“Bradley has not played a single minute since the World Cup, so we needed to be careful. I’m happy because 30 minutes is going to be good for his fitness for his build-up, and we will continue because now we play a lot of games. So he will have the chance to play.

‌



"I think two points also don't reflect our two first games. So definitely, we couldn't lose anymore and I’m happy because I think we controlled it well today.”

Ipswich boss Gary O’Neil insisted he was happy with his team and “proud of his players.” He added: “After the first two goals, we recovered and matched them and were arguably the better team at times.”

Sports.title: Virgil van Dijk makes feelings very clear on Cody Gakpo after Liverpool exit U-turn
Sports.content:
Virgil van Dijk makes feelings very clear on Cody Gakpo after Liverpool exit U-turn

Cody Gakpo has been key to Liverpool so far under Andoni Iraola but the Dutchman might not have been at Anfield after all had a move to Manchester City been completed over the final days of the window

View 2 Images

Virgil van Dijk insists Cody Gakpo will continue to be crucial to Liverpool after his failed move to Manchester City. The Dutchman was thought to be on the way out of Anfield over the final days of the transfer window.

‌



Tottenham Hotspur had been credited as admirers, only to be gazumped by Premier League rivals Manchester City. Gakpo even went as far as approving a switch to the Etihad Stadium.

‌



But for various reasons - including Liverpool’s inability to find a replacement - his switch was not completed. The Reds might be thankful of that fact given how key the Dutch forward has been to Liverpool.

‌



He netted on the opening day of the season and followed that up with an assist against Nottingham Forest. Gakpo then set up Alexander Isak twice against Ipswich on Friday evening.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Speaking after that game, club and international teammate Virgil van Dijk was full of praise. Asked how important Gakpo has been, he said: “Massively.

‌



“Obviously I said before the transfer window was closed that he’s important for us and he will be important for us this season as well. And he showed it again today. Last week as well with the assists, over the last couple of years as well. So keep going.”

Isak’s comments are very similar to that of Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola, who suggested that he had no doubts over the forward’s commitment. Speaking ahead of the trip to Portman Road, the Spanish coach said: "My relationship with Cody has been very honest from the beginning.

“He has played very well for us so far. He was always aware of the situation in the market, we were constantly talking, I hope we can keep him at the same level. He is in a good place physically and mentally and I'm very happy to pick him."

‌



View 2 Images Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo linked up well at Ipswich (Image: Getty Images)

Gakpo now appears set to remain at Liverpool until January at least - and Liverpool fans will be hopeful that his fledgling partnership with Isak will continue to improve.

Speaking about his understanding with the Swedish forward, Isak said: “We will see. Obviously as attackers, we always train with each other and try and get to know each other even better again. Hopefully we can assist each other many times so he owes me a few assists now.”

Sports.title: Liverpool transfer call vindicated as Alexander Isak downs Ipswich - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Liverpool finally secured their first win of the Premier League season by beating newly-promoted Ipswich at Portman Road.

Liverpool took control early on through Alexander Isak as he scored twice in the opening ten minutes. The Reds thought they were set to be handed a penalty after Dominik Szoboszlai was fouled midway through the second-half but VAR correctly intervened.

But the damage was already done in the first half by Isak, as Liverpool sealed their first success of the campaign, while it's now back-to-back defeats for Ipswich.

Here are all of the talking points from Portman Road:

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Isak back to his best

Barely six minutes into the game and Liverpool were ahead through Isak. A lot of the praise for the goal has to go to Cody Gakpo, who showed great feet in the centre of the park and picked out the Swedish forward with an inch-perfect ball.

He controlled and then hammered past Kjell Scherpen in the Ipswich goal, who may have thought he could have done better. But Isak will not care too much, having netted his second goal of the season.

Two became three barely three minutes later as he latched onto another brilliant pass by Gakpo, composed himself and slotted home. He's now matched his Premier League goal record from the entirety of last season and it would be foolish to bet against him beating that.

‌



He actually thought he had done after getting on the end of a Florian Wirtz cross but had drifted offside.

View 3 Images Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo linked up well at Ipswich (Image: Getty Images)

Gakpo call spot on

If things had panned out differently, Liverpool might not have had Cody Gakpo's services to call upon for this game. He appeared set for a move to Manchester City over the closing days of the window.

For one reason or another, the move did not come to fruition. Liverpool will be hugely thankful that it didn't. Gakpo's passes for Isak were brilliant - the first being an inch-perfect pass, the second being a brilliant, outside of the boot effort.

‌



Like Isak, Gakpo has really impressed over the opening weeks of the campaign and that was certainly the same at Portman Road.

Penalty decision explained

Liverpool thought they were going to be given a golden opportunity to extend their lead even further as Dominik Szoboszlai was taken down by Leif Davies.

The referee did not give the decision initially but looked as though he would change his mind upon review. But the hosts still had a reprieve, with the Liverpool midfielder offside in the build-up, rendering the controversy irrelevant in any case.

It might not have been the call that Liverpool wanted, but it was the correct one.

‌



View 3 Images Dominik Szoboszlai thought he had won a penalty against Ipswich (Image: Getty Images)

Barcola gets Premier League introduction

While Liverpool fans will have been keen to see their side win, another key moment that they were looking forward to was Bradley Barcola's debut. The Frenchman was named on the bench following his £123m move from PSG.

But he came on in the second period to make his bow. In honesty, he was on the periphery of the game but there were a few moments where he showed his electric pace in front of the away fans so they will certainly be keen to see that a lot more throughout his time on Merseyside.

First win, first clean sheet

Liverpool's defensive frailties have been well discussed this season. And they were on show once again at Portman Road. The hosts managed to get through on a few occasions, with it taking either an important intervention from Jeremy Jacquet or a save from Alisson to keep them out.

‌



Regardless, Liverpool finally have their first win and first clean sheet of the campaign and that will be a big relief to Andoni Iraola.

When it comes to Ipswich, their season will of course not be defined against games against Liverpool - or indeed last week's trip to Old Trafford - so they won't be too worried at all.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso rubs salt in Arsenal wounds over Morgan Rogers transfer ahead of clash
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso rubs salt in Arsenal wounds over Morgan Rogers transfer ahead of clash

Arsenal were linked with a big-money move for Morgan Rogers earlier this summer only to see Premier League rivals Chelsea swoop in and seal a deal instead for an eye-watering £117m

View 2 Images Morgan Rogers has had a bright starts to life with Chelsea (Image: Getty Images)

Xabi Alonso has hailed Morgan Rogers for his impact at Chelsea after beating Arsenal to his services. The England star completed a £117m move to Stamford Bridge in July.

‌



He has had a brilliant start to life in West London, having netted his first goal for the club in the opening day win against Fulham, while he also notched an assist in the 4-3 victory against Brighton.

‌



Speaking about the playmaker’s form, Alonso has praised the 24-year-old for his positive start and pointed to how much of a statement his arrival was.

‌



Speaking in his pre-match press conference ahead of this weekend’s clash with Arsenal, Alonso said: “For sure, Morgan was a big, big one to get a player of his stature - in the present and future. He will be a key player for the next six, seven years. He's had a great impact."

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

While Arsenal did not manage to sign Rogers, they still spent heavily on their team. Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimaraes, Ezri Konsa and Piero Hincapie all arrived for big fees.

‌



But Gunners icon Ian Wright has bemoaned the fact that they didn’t manage to get a deal over the line for Rogers. “I think we did need Rogers,” Wright said on Stick to Football.

“It’s not a disastrous window but if I’m Mikel (Arteta), I wouldn’t be happy with how this window has gone simply because we’ve gone another window where we have not got that forward.

View 2 Images Xabi Alonso has been full of praise for Morgan Rogers (Image: Getty Images)

‌



“Mikel has talked about getting players to take us to that level, he did it again after Paris, where we didn’t have that player to break them. That is the player Mikel wanted. They chased Vini until the end of the earth and left Morgan Rogers dangling.”

He added: “You say we have got those types of players but that is what Mikel wanted. It is a position where we need that player. Of course Saka is back, Odegaard is back, Havertz is back and playing together, but he wanted that difference-maker.

“He [Rogers] is the one we were linked with ages ago and he would have loved to have come, I can feel it.

Article continues below

“There’s something that’s happened with Arsenal with the way they were going for Vini. If you’re a player and you see a team going for him, you think, ‘I thought they were interested in me?’. It is the player the manager wanted. Chelsea thought, well if you’re not going to pay it, we’ll pay it. I’m gutted, I would have loved him to come.”

Sports.title: Michael Carrick hints he could fill problem Man Utd position without spending a penny
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick hints he could fill problem Man Utd position without spending a penny

Manchester United spent just under £150m in the summer transfer window but the Red Devils still have one specific position in the squad that could cause an issue for the remainder of the season

View 2 Images Michael Carrick did not manage to sign a left-back this summer (Image: Getty Images)

Michael Carrick has not ruled out Patrick Dorgu being a solution to his left-back headache this season. The Red Devils had the position as one to strengthen this summer, having been linked with a few options.

‌



Barcelona’s Alejandro Balde was mentioned, while the Red Devils made a late play for Manchester City star Rayan Ait-Nouri. Neither of those moves came to fruition, leaving just Luke Shaw as Carrick’s only senior option at left-back.

‌



Harry Amass was linked with a loan move away from Old Trafford on deadline day but the decision was made to keep him. Asked if winger Dorgu could be an option going forwards, United boss Carrick is not against the idea.

‌



"He can certainly play there. He has done, without doubt," said Carrick. "I'm not sitting here saying he can't do that. It's just the way we've been since I've been here.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"He actually has been injured, unfortunately, for some time. You could almost argue that he played three or four times for us last season, so for me, he's almost like a new player, you know, to have, and it's almost like a new signing in some ways because he's added so much to the group."

‌



"He's played off the right for Denmark, scored a great goal in the summer playing off the right in a forward position," the United boss added. "He can play left-back. He's that type where he can do a number of things. I'm certainly not saying he can't do that at all.

"It's something he can, we just haven't had to explore that. At some point, we might have to, at some point he might do that. He can do that, absolutely no problem. There are times in training when he does it.

View 2 Images Dorgu has played out wide for the majority of his career at Manchester United (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"And then he's only young, being such a young age and having the attributes that he's got, we've just got to keep trying to get the most out of him."

Dorgu arrived at Old Trafford from Italian side Lecce in 2025 and he has gone on to make 50 appearances in all for the Red Devils, albeit just a handful of those have come in defence.

While United did not manage to get a left-back, it was a busy summer in all, especially when it comes to midfield. The club spent around £140m on a midfield rebuild, with Youri Tielemans, Carlos Baleba and Andrey Santos all arriving.

Article continues below

It is now thought that United chiefs will look to bolster their defence next summer, with Newcastle's Lewis Hall potentially among the options that could be considered.

Sports.title: Greaves makes more history with win at Czech Darts Open
Sports.content:
Beau Greaves made more darting history as she became the first woman to win a match on the PDC's European Tour - a feat that secured her a second-round clash with Luke Humphries at the Czech Darts Open.

The 22-year-old rallied from 3-1 down to beat Daryl Gurney 6-4 in Prague on Friday night and will now play world No 2 Humphries in the last-32 on Saturday evening, with the winner meeting Nathan Aspinall or Andrew Gilding in round three on Sunday afternoon.

Greaves' latest landmark moment follows becoming the first woman to hit a nine-darter on the PDC Pro Tour, against Mensur Suljovic back in February, and the first to win a PDC ranking title, doing so when she edged Michael Smith 8-7 at Players Championship 11.

She was also the first woman to qualify for a European Tour event when she reached last month's Hungarian Darts Trophy.

Image: Gurney had pipped Greaves in a first-round match at the 2026 World Darts Championship at Alexandra Palace (Pic credit: PDC)

Greaves lost to Rob Cross in the first round in Budapest despite averaging 104 but her run in Prague will now last at least one more match after pinning double one to defeat Gurney, a player she had suffered a narrow 3-2 loss to in round one of the 2026 World Championship.

Greaves 'loving the experience', will 'be ready' for Humphries

Greaves said after a contest in which she won three straight legs in 14, 13 and 11 darts: "It feels amazing. It's just so nice to win a game, I was so nervous at the start, I don't know why. It took me so long to get settled.

"It means loads to me, the crowd's fantastic. It's such a tight stage and you feel so much from the crowd. I'm really enjoying it and loving the experience."

The Yorkshirewoman showed tremendous fight to respond from an early two-leg deficit once Gurney produced a 144 checkout - the same finish which had helped him see off Greaves at Alexandra Palace late last year.

Image: Luke Humphries is Greaves' second-round opponent in Prague

On facing Humphries next, a player she met at the 2025 UK Open, Greaves added: "I've played Luke on the big stage before so I know what to expect, he's world class so I'm going to have to play a lot better than I did tonight.

"What more do you want than on a Euro Tour to play one of the best players in the world? I'll look forward to it and I'll be ready."

Littler to begin campaign on Saturday

Elsewhere on Friday, Niko Springer averaged 102 while routing Martin Homola 6-0 to book a second-round meeting with world No 1 Luke Littler.

Springer said of his showdown with Littler: "I have nothing to lose to be honest. I'm feeling very confident. Of course it will be hard, but it's best of 11, so let's go, I'm ready."

Image: Luke Littler gets his Czech Darts Open campaign under way on Saturday against Niko Springer

Joe Cullen, Dirk van Duijvenbode and Cross were big-name casualties, dumped out by Stephen Burton, Mario Vandenbogaerde and Keane Barry respectively.

Humphries, who, like Littler, received a bye to round two as one of the 16 seeded players, has won the last two Czech Darts Open titles, thrashing Kim Huybrechets 8-1 in the 2024 final and then seeing off Josh Rock 8-5 last year.

'Cool Hand' is targeting a fourth victory in five years at this event having overcome Cross 8-5 in the 2022 final.

Michael van Gerwen and Gerwyn Price are also among the seeds in Prague and will take on Vandenbogaerde and Callan Rydz respectively on Saturday night in the Czech capital.

Sports.title: Hunt runs season's best to take third in Diamond League 200m
Sports.content:
Amy Hunt: British sprinter runs season's best 200m time to take third in Diamond League Athletics meet in Brussels

Great Britain's Amy Hunt ran a season's best in the women's 200m at the final Diamond League event of the year as she took third place in Brussels

Great Britain's Amy Hunt ran a season's best in the women's 200m at the final Diamond League event of the year as she took third place in Brussels.

Hunt's time of 22.16 was outstripped by race winner - and reigning Olympic 100m champion - Julien Alfred of St Lucia (21.79) and America's Kayla White (22.00).

Another Brit, Success Eduan, came seventh of the eight runners after clocking 23.06 in Belgium.

Hunt won four gold medals at the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham this summer

Hunt was the poster girl of the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham this summer with her four gold medals and bubbly personality winning her legions of fans.

The 24-year-old topped the podium individually in the 100m and 200m in the Midlands, while she won gold as part of the women's and mixed 4x100m relays.

Elsewhere in Brussels on Friday night, European 400m men's gold medalist Matthew Hudson-Smith, of Great Britain, finished fifth in his event.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

Duplantis in injury scare ahead of World Athletics Ultimate Championships

Sweden's pole vault world record-holder Armand Duplantis was forced to pull out of the Diamond League final with back tightness, a week before the inaugural World ‌Athletics Ultimate Championships in Budapest.

Duplantis said: "The worst possible thing to do is having to pull out of a competition. The fans wanted to see a good show and I wish I could deliver that. Unfortunately, I can't right now.

"My head is everywhere right now. It's super difficult, but that's life, that's the life of an athlete. I try to stay calm and positive. We will see if I can make the Ultimate Championships. I don't have the answer right now."

The World Athletics Ultimate Championships is a new biennial event which sees world champions, Olympic champions, Diamond League winners and other leading athletes compete against each other for shares of a $10m (£7.87m) purse.

Armand Duplantis' army of fans will hope he is fit for the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championships in Budapest next weekend

Each individual ​champion will secure $150,000 (£110,865), the biggest winner's ​cheque in track and field history.

Noah Lyles, the men's 100m champion at the 2024 Paris Olympics, will not take part, having ended his season early due to injury - but he still plans to travel to Hungary.

"I am still ​going to be at Ultimate Championship. I still do have ​parties to throw and things to do behind the scenes to help support ​the athletes," Lyles said.

"I still think that this is going to be an ⁠amazing competition, and I'm excited to watch that. And I'm even more excited to see what the future is going to bring."

Sports.title: How influencers at US Open are testing boundaries of tennis etiquette
Sports.content:
A huge discussion around tennis etiquette has been sparked at the US Open due to the disruption caused by a growing number of content creators and influencers at Flushing Meadows.

The number of content creators who have been accredited to cover this year's final Grand Slam of the year has doubled from last year in a move by organisers to reach new audiences. Yet the noise and disturbance caused by them in the stands as been felt by players on court.

Chair umpire Kader Nouni admonished a group of influencers in a suite for recording a video in the middle of a point, while another incident saw a creator using the use of a bright portable ring light to take photos.

Meanwhile, in Naomi Osaka's second-round victory, chair umpire Marijana Veljovic asked fans several times to be quiet.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Naomi Broady and Ryan Harrison try to teach some UK influencers how to play tennis at the US Open

Some players have questioned whether the push for online engagement has gone too far with two-time champion Osaka saying: "I think obviously if you come to a sporting event, you have to respect the sport.".

"I feel like it's common courtesy to read up on the sport, especially the etiquette."

The US Open introduced a policy of free fan movement in 2024, meaning spectators no longer have to wait to take their seats during changeovers.

And since Osaka's opening match, there has been increased messaging on screens reminding people to refrain from any activity that could disrupt the game, including noise levels, flash photography and ring lights.

Some of the behaviour 'disrespectful'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports tennis panel discusses the best fashion so far at the US Open

American and third seed Jessica Pegula has said some of the behaviour has been "disrespectful".

"I can appreciate the influencers coming and showcasing the US Open experience," she said. "But I do think that it's tough when you see videos when they're taking pictures and using the selfie lights.

"People are down there trying to perform. It's their career and their job. It seems a bit disrespectful."

Celebrities have long been ubiquitous in the stands - from A-list stars to US President Donald Trump - as the ultra-wealthy shell out thousands of dollars for seats to get through Flushing Meadows' doors.

But the growing love affair between influencers and the premier ⁠American tennis event has caused some growing pains.

World No 4 Coco Gauff welcomed the influx of new fans but said they should respect the traditions of tennis.

"I definitely think it's cool to have a new demographic and I definitely think it helps grow the sport," she said.

"But if you're being invited to a red carpet, you wouldn't show up in jeans.

"I think it's just follow the etiquette of the sport."

'We all want tennis to grow'

Eliza Wastcoat is an influencer who has a passion and knowledge for tennis. She has even launched her own social media channel exploring the intersection of tennis and fashion.

Wastcoat, who moved to America to attend the prestigious Lehigh University, and began her professional career at a creative agency, believes there is room to grow the game but only if organisers and influencers can work together.

"There is a space in tennis for influencers and content creators to be welcomed into the sport and reach new audiences, but I think there's ways in which the sport can do that which includes content creators and influencers who appreciate the sport itself and the etiquette of it and for those who are maybe new and are bringing new audiences in," said Wastcoat, who served as a Wimbledon ball kid when she was younger.

"I do think it's the responsibility of both the brands, the tournaments and the individuals coming to read up a little bit and understand the etiquette of the type of sporting event they're going to.

"Tennis has really opened up its doors to change but ultimately players need some quiet and the ability to concentrate.

"We all want tennis to grow so inviting people in and making it an all-round experience is great for the game, so it's just an opportunity to further educate people about the game on what tennis is."

A learning curve for the USTA

The United States Tennis Association said it wanted fans to have an "incredible time" while ensuring they did not interfere with the action.

"We are continually looking for ways to ensure fans in the stands know what is permitted and what is prohibited," read a statement from the governing body.

Sports.title: Lawrence leads at halfway stage in Switzerland as he aims to emulate Ballesteros
Sports.content:
Defending champion Thriston Lawrence reeled off six birdies in a row and then made an excellent par save from a bunker to secure the lead at the halfway stage of the Omega European Masters as he looks to emulate the late, great Seve Ballesteros.

Ballesteros is the only player to win this event three times since it became a DP World Tour tournament in 1972, doing so in 1977, 1978 and 1989 - but Lawrence has a chance to do likewise having triumphed at Crans-sur-Siere in 2022 and then again last season.

The South African carded a bogey-free, seven-under 63 on Friday to reach 13 under par and take a two-shot advantage over Germany's Jeremy Paul and Spain's Ignacio Elvira - who shot a round-of-the-day 62 - into the weekend in Switzerland.

Japan's Keita Nakajima sits fourth on 10 under with England's Paul Casey among a group of three players in a share of fifth on nine under with 36 holes remaining.

Casey's compatriot Harry Hall reached 10 under through nine holes of his second round after five front-nine birdies saw him go out in 30, only for a hip injury to then hamper him as he bogeyed three of his final five and slipped to seven under, six shots off the pace.

Image: Lawrence is a five-time winner on the DP World Tour, including twice at the Omega European Masters

Lawrence: I've been playing well all year

Starting at the 10th, Lawrence parred five of his first six holes around a birdie at 13 before he ignited from the 16th when a superb tee shot left him a tap-in birdie.

The 29-year-old picked up shots at his next five holes, too, with highlights including draining from over 40 feet at the first and then holing from off the green at the second.

Lawrence was unable to add to his birdie haul across the last third of his round but saved par at five when he chipped in from the sand - his second attempt to get out of that hazard having initially used the putter to no avail.

Lawrence, without a top-10 finish since March, said afterwards: "I've played well all year. I've just been unfortunate so many times, missing the cut by one shot four or five times. I feel like I've been playing well, but mentally, I'm in a much better space.

"Seeing birdies and putts go in, I feel like you gain confidence from that. Coming back to a place I love is just extra confidence."

Sports.title: Star-studded London City cruise to win over Man Utd
Sports.content:
London City Lionesses started their star-studded era and the new Women's Super League season with a comfortable 2-1 win over Manchester United.

Two-time Ballon d'Or winner Alexia Putellas made her debut for the club but despite the Spain international drawing a sell-out crowd at Hayes Lane, it was an own goal from Julia Zigiotti that opened the scoring.

The midfielder wrestled with Alanna Kennedy in the box before inadvertently guiding a header into the back of her own net to score the first goal of the 2026/27 campaign.

London City cruised into control of the fixture from there on, keeping United at arm's length throughout, before a moment of magic from Danielle van de Donk with a neat flick doubled the lead and sealed all three points for the hosts with under 10 minutes to go.

United substitute Simi Awujo tucked away a late consolation goal with virtually the last kick of the game and their only shot on target, highlighting the chasm in standards between the two sides with the talent London City now have at their disposal.

Rosa Kafaji, Mapi Leon, Putellas and Janni Thomsen were the fresh faces included and impressed - while Mary Earps and Kadidiatou Diani were unused on the bench - as an exciting new era got off to the perfect start while owner Michele Kang watched from the stands.

The key moments from Hayes Lane...

9: GOAL! Zigiotti's own goal gives London City the lead

49: SAVE! Kafaji forces a good save from Tullis-Joyce with a long-range shot

64: INJURY! Lucia Corrales goes off injured while clutching shoulder

82: SUPERB! Van den Donk's flick doubles London City's lead to seal three points

90+10: CONSOLATION! Awujo grabs late goal with United's only shot on target

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Simi Awujo smashes it home to grab a late goal for Manchester United against London City Lionesses.

Maestre: We were very dominant

London City Lionesses boss Eder Maestre:

"Starting with a win is very important to keep building confidence.

"I think we were very dominant through the whole game. I really think we deserved this win. I hope this kind of result makes the difference in the way we can keep playing in the next games we have.

"That's the identity we want - that's why I'm very proud of the team.

"Sometimes you need to take some risks to play in that way. The team played with the togetherness that I think are going to be the most important value to respect.

"I think we are one step closer to hitting the targets. I'm very excited and very happy."

'We were not us,' says Olid

Manchester United boss Eva Olid:

"I think none of us are happy with the first half. We were not us.

"Nothing that we have been working on was happening in the first half.

"In the half-time, it was me saying to them, this is not us, we need to have confidence, belief, show we want the ball, that has to be us.

"There was a change in the second half but at the end but I said at the end that needs to be 90 minutes. It's not enough just 40 minutes trying to have the ball."

Sports.title: 'Let's go one more time' - Taylor bows out from boxing at 'dream' venue
Sports.content:
Katie Taylor's glittering boxing career will draw to a close on Saturday night at her "dream venue" and with the message a simple one: "Let's go one more time".

Taylor will aim to retire as a three-time undisputed world champion when she takes on unbeaten Frenchwoman Flora Pili in front of 80,000 fans at Croke Park in Dublin.

The 40-year-old, who weighed in at 139.6lbs for the super-lightweight showdown compared to Pili's 139.9lbs, has pretty much done it all in boxing.

Her accolades including winning Olympic gold in London in 2012 and, along with Amanda Serrano, becoming the first woman to headline a fight card at New York's iconic Madison Square ‌Garden.

She also avenged her sole pro defeat, against Chantelle Cameron.

But she has never fought at Croke Park before - until now.

Image: Pili (right) has a 12-0 record as a pro

'This is what I was born for, this is what I was made for'

While fight week, quite rightly, has seen the great and good of boxing and beyond praise Taylor's career, hail the inspiration she has been and discuss the legacy she will leave, the woman herself is not looking beyond Pili.

Speaking shortly after hitting the scales on Friday evening, the Bray Bomber, said: "My mind is focused on the fight. I have a job to do against a very tough challenger.

"I have built my reputation on always taking the tough fights, so why treat my last fight any differently? This is what I was born for, this is what I was made for. Let's go one more time."

Taylor did, though, turn to address her fans at the weigh-in, many of whom will also be rooting for her inside the stadium this weekend.

"I am blown away. I want to put on a performance worthy of the support I have had these last few years

"You guys have carried me throughout the Olympics and my whole career. Thank you so much. I am so grateful.

"I am so excited. I have been dreaming about this for the last few years and I am one day away from ending my career in a dream venue in front of all these amazing people."

Image: Katie Taylor has only lost once as a pro, a defeat to Chantelle Cameron that she went on to avenge

'Katie is an absolute hero to so many people'

Former world champion Carl Frampton, speaking on DAZN, feels the lure of a bout at Saturday's prolonged Taylor's time as an active fighter.

He said: "She has completed the sport but I think one of the reasons she held on was the dream of fighting at Croke Park. She has finally got it.

"Katie is an absolute hero to so many people, an inspiration. It is a perfect way to finish - but she has to win first and we can't rule out Pili who is a very good fighter."

But is it definitely it for Taylor - or is a return to the ring possible?

Three-weight world champion Mikaela Mayer added: "Katie has always been very true to her word.

"If she says this is her last fight, I believe it to be. If she wants to come back, I would not be upset about it. We'd love to see her again.

"I am benefitting off of her hard work and everything she has helped create for the women in this sport. I am sad as I had always hoped to share the ring with Katie."

Sports.title: Sabalenka complains of cannabis smell during win as Alcaraz progresses
Sports.content:
Aryna Sabalenka complained to the umpire about a strong ​smell of cannabis that was present duing her third-round win over Kamilla Rakhimova at the US Open.

The world No 1 came through in straight sets, beating her unseeded opponent 6-3 6-4 on Louis Armstrong Stadium, but after racing into a 3-0 lead in the opening set, Sabalenka complained to umpire Eva Asderaki-Moore at the first changeover.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player World number one Aryna Sabalenka stopped her US Open match against Kamilla Rakhimova due to a 'strong' smell of cannabis

"I was like, 'Guys, you can do whatever, you can smoke whatever, you can relax as much as you can, but please to not do it around ‌the tennis courts'," Sabalenka told reporters afterwards. "It's a bit tricky to handle that smell while you're trying to compete at your best."

No fans were found to be smoking and ejected from the tennis grounds.

Sabalenka added: "I don't know if it was coming from the crowd or was from the outside, because the wind blows it into the stadium. I don't know. I just hope they're going to be a bit more aware of that stuff."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aryna Sabalenka' spoke about the 'disruption' following her brief halt of play during her US Open match against Kamilla Rakhimova due to a 'strong' smell of cannabis

US Tennis Association spokesman Brendan McIntyre said in a statement: "While we can't control what takes place off the grounds of the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center, we continue to be vigilant as we maintain this facility as a smoke free environment."

The distraction didn't affect Sabalenka's form in the slightest as she didn't miss a single first serve until the seventh game of the match, in which Rakhimova would three times take her to deuce.

That would prove to be Rakhimova's only real opening in the first set, Sabalenka taking it 6-3, but she'd prove much more competitive in the second.

Rakhimova came from behind four-straight times to hold serve, saving four break points along the way, before Sabalenka finally ended her resolve in the ninth game of the second set.

On this occasion, Rakhimova let a 40-0 lead slip as the four-time Grand Slam champion battled back to secure the crucial break before serving things out to book her spot in the last 16.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Naomi Osaka, Jessica Pegula and Coco Gauff weigh in on influencers disrupting matches at the US Open

Sabalenka 'shuts down outside noise' to book Townsend meeting

After Sabalenka's second-round win, she cut short questions about her pre-tournament activities in an excruciating exchange with a reporter.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aryna Sabalenka was quick to highlight that everything she does off-court is worked around her tennis schedule

A regular poster on social media at the various events she attends and with the brands she works, Sabalenka fired back that her off-court appearances had not come at the expense of her preparations ​for Flushing Meadows.

Referencing that further after her victory over Rakhimova, Sabalenka added: "I completely shut down noise from outside.

"I focus on myself, and I know if I do that and work really hard I will have my chances and be able to play a great level of tennis."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aryna Sabalenka was left furious over questions during her press conference at the US Open following her round-two victory, as one reporter asked her about her pre-tournament 'partying'

Trying to become the first player to win three-straight US Open titles since Serena Williams from 2012-14, Sabalenka will face American Taylor Townsend in the last 16 after she beat 13th seed Diana Shnaider 6-2 6-7 (3-7) 6-3

Jessica Pegula kept alive her bid ‌for a maiden Grand Slam title when the third seed rallied from behind ‌to beat fellow former US Open finalist Leylah Fernandez 1-6 ​6-4 6-3.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Jessica Pegula vs Leylah Fernandez against from the US Open

The American will face Romania's Sorana Cirstea ​in the last 16 after the 16th seed defeated Italy Jasmine Paolini in straight sets 6-3 6-3.

Alcaraz overcomes mid-match wobble to reach fourth round

Defending men's champion Carlos Alcaraz continued his impressive comeback after more than four months out to a wrist injury, as he beat Wu Yibing in straight sets, 6-3 6-4 6-1, on Arthur Ashe Stadium.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the US Open match between Carlos Alcaraz and Yibing Wu

The seven-time Grand Slam champion was made to work harder than the scoreline suggests, however, as he was broken back in both the first two sets by his 113th-ranked opponent.

The second set, in particular, was cause for frustration for the Spaniard as he appeared to be cruising along at 2-0 up after winning five games in a row, only to again be pegged back by Wu.

Alcaraz would finally earn another break of serve in the 10th game to clinch a two-set lead before he finally pulled clear in the third.

"In the toughest moments I did everything good, which I'm really happy about," Alcaraz said in his on-court interview. "Could it be better? Yes. But overall I'm just really proud and happy with the performance today.

"To be honest, I'm playing better than I thought [after wrist injury]. Physically, I thought I was going to be dead after the first match. But I'm recovering really well.

"My level right now is really good, I've got the rhythm of the competition every time I step on the court."

Alcaraz will face American 20th seed Tommy Paul ‌in the last 16 after he emerged victorious from a five-set thriller against Kazakhstan's 15th seed Alexander Bublik, winning 6-4 3-6 6-7 (4-7) 6-1 6-3 in a match that lasted three hours and 13 minutes.

Elsewhere, seventh seed, and 2021 US Open champion, Daniil Medvedev overpowered Frenchman Arthur ‌Rinderknech with a 6-4 6-4 6-4 victory.

Sports.title: 'It's going to be tight' - Hamilton eyes 'dream' Monza pole
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton is predicting a “very close” battle in Italian Grand Prix qualifying on Saturday for what he says would he says would be a “dream” pole position at Monza.

Hamilton was outperformed by his Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc in both of Friday's practice sessions but the team's overall performance, following the arrival of a new engine upgrade, suggested they have the pace to compete for pole.

Leclerc topped Hamilton in first practice before Mercedes' George Russell was fastest in the second session, with Leclerc second and Hamilton only fifth behind Kimi Antonelli and McLaren's Lando Norris.

Ferrari are set to go into qualifying, live on Sky Sports F1 at 3pm, with a two-versus-one advantage over Mercedes due to world championship leader Kimi Antonelli having already incurred penalties for exceeding his engine-part allowance that will see him start from the back of the grid regardless of where he finishes the session.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from Friday's practice sessions at the Italian Grand Prix.

"It's going to be tight, it's very close," Hamilton said. "We're up against the McLarens and the Mercedes, they are very, very competitive.

"Every weekend the Mercedes is just really, really quick. It'll be tough, for sure, but we need to knuckle down tonight and see if we can pull something out."

Asked about the possibility of starting on the front row or pole position at Ferrari's home race, Hamilton replied: "That's the dream, the ultimate dream.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton arrived at the Italian GP in a rare Ferrari F40 and revealed that the car's engine bore the same number as his racing number.

"Whether or not we can is the big, big question. And that's going to take a lot of work tonight to try to figure out if we've gone wrong anywhere and if there's any places we can improve, which there are loads of places we can improve.

"Also, I think being in the right place at the right time on track is going to help a lot."

Antonelli predicts 'tight fight' for pole

Despite not being a factor in the pole contest, Antonelli agrees with Hamilton's assessment that it will be a tight battle.

The 20-year-old Italian leads both Russell and Hamilton by 59 points at the top of the standings, with Norris trailing by 83 points in fourth.

Mercedes have chosen Antonelli's home race as the most suitable venue for him to serve an inevitable penalty for exceeding his engine allowance, due to a belief that fighting back through the field in Sunday's race will be easier at Monza than most other tracks that remain on this year's schedule.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes Kimi Antonelli gives his thoughts on Ferrari after they debuted a new engine at the Italian GP practice sessions.

Antonelli said: "Today a bit of a different day compared to usual. A lot more focused on long runs so it was a bit weird, not going to lie, but overall, it was a good day.

"We gathered a lot of data and now looking forward to the next few days.

"Ferrari definitely took a step forward with a new engine and now the speeds are the same. We know how good their car is into the corners so, for sure, it's going to be a tight fight for pole tomorrow."

'Struggling' Norris doesn't expect to fight for pole

Norris arrived in Italy full of confidence having claimed back-to-back victories in Hungary and the Netherlands to reignite his hopes of defending his drivers' title.

However, the Brit was downcast after McLaren appeared unable to replicate their recent form at a track with very different characteristics to the previous two on the schedule.

Norris said: "Not very decent. Just struggling a lot more with pace.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A downbeat Lando Norris reflects on McLaren’s frustrating lack of pace in Friday Practice.

"In the corners we expected to be good at we're bad at and in the corners we expected to be bad at, we're not so bad at.

"But we're still off. So not in a great place at the minute. We'll see what we can do overnight but it's going to be tougher than before for sure.



"It's close between a lot of the guys at the top. The guys behind are not that far either so they can easily surprise us.

"I definitely don't feel we are in the fight for pole at all but we need to focus on getting a decent result."

Sports.title: Isak’s rapid double sinks Ipswich to give Andoni Iraola first Liverpool win
Sports.content:
A first win for Andoni Iraola’s Liverpool, the introduction of the latest star signing in Bradley Barcola making for a successful Friday night. Better yet, continuing signs that Alexander Isak, last year’s model, is coming back to life, his two, well-taken early goals securing the three points. That Cody Gakpo, Isak’s supplier, might have been at Manchester City or Tottenham had the transfer runes been right, added further to a sense of renewal. Liverpool’s attackers were full of the speed and invention sorely lacking for much of last season.

Once Barcola arrived in the second half, those velocity levels increased yet further, Liverpool playing the attacking style, high on risk and entertainment, the appointment of Iraola promised. “We are starting to get to the way we want to play,” said Isak afterwards.

Travelling Liverpool fans were made to wait for their first glimpse of £123m Barcola, his being on the bench adding further suspense to a deal that took an entire summer to complete.

If Ipswich looked to show the “emotional discipline” their manager, Gary O’Neil, said they lacked in losing 5-2 at Old Trafford, little was in evidence in a ruinous opening spell that betrayed the decent performance they went on to put in.

How long will Iraola’s doctrines take to embed? Perhaps not as long as feared. Isak, the most expensive player signed under the outgoing sporting director Richard Hughes, looks – at last – to be flowering. To follow his strike against Nottingham Forest, he had scored twice by the 10th minute. “If Alex is fit and is available, he will produce the numbers,” said Iraola.

Assisted for both by Gakpo, the finishes were of the gold standard Liverpool invested so heavily in. “Cody was outstanding,” said Virgil van Dijk, sharing the credit. “I said it before the transfer window had closed, he’s important for us, and he will be important this season.” Iraola joined the appreciation society: “I had no doubt with Cody … he knows how much we value him.”

“The level is ruthless,” said O’Neil, otherwise exalted by his team’s response to adversity beyond those opening nine minutes. “If you make mistakes against players like Gakpo, Wirtz and Barcola, there’s a chance you will get punished.”

Just as at Old Trafford, two Ipswich goals were conceded in quick, damaging succession, the defence far too open and chaotic. After Víctor Muñoz had set off on a long run stopped only by Issa Diop’s last-man tackle, Julio Enciso controlled the ball, taking a beat by standing on the ball, as if calling for calm.

Isak, who had a third first-half goal disallowed for offside, made the runs into scoring positions that made his reputation, nothing like the sorry figure of his debut, lost season. Meanwhile, a no-look pass from Ipswich’s captain, Dara O’Shea, straight to Gakpo, betrayed a collective cognitive dissonance.

View image in fullscreen Bradley Barcola beats Dara O’Shea on his Liverpool debut. Photograph: Dave Shopland/AP

Florian Wirtz becoming involved with the tricks and flicks offered another pointer that last summer’s huge Liverpool outlay may not be so wasteful as it appeared in Arne Slot’s dog days. Iraola’s appointment came with a reputation for improving players. Should the Basque get the best from the German, in a similar price bracket to Barcola and Isak, then this week’s pronouncement he is happy with his squad will ring truer.
