World.title: Estonia terminates Ukraine arms deals worth over €71 million, pursues court cases
World.content:
The Estonian Center for Defense Investments (RKIK) has so far concluded 27 contracts intended to purchase weapons or ammunition for Ukraine. Of the 27 contracts, seven have been terminated, and RKIK has already taken five of them to court.

Elmar Vaher, head of the Estonian Center for Defense Investments, said on ERR's morning show Friday that RKIK has concluded 28 contracts, eight of which are currently problematic.

Later, RKIK's media relations expert clarified that due to human error a mistake had appeared in the tables, and in fact there are 27 contracts in total, of which seven have been terminated. The total value of all 27 contracts is roughly 350 million euros.

"In the case of these (problematic contracts – ed.), it can be said that they have not gone as we wished, that the goods would reach Ukraine," Vaher said.

For four contracts concluded with one company, RKIK turned to international arbitration. For one joint contract concluded by two companies, RKIK turned to Harju District Court. The total value of these contracts is 59.8 million euros.

In addition, RKIK has terminated two more contracts concluded with two companies, for which materials are also being prepared to turn to court. The total value of these contracts is 11.8 million euros.

Court proceedings expected in this and next year

According to the head of RKIK, it is difficult to assess whether the standard for concluding procurements was lower before his term.

Riigi kaitseinvesteeringute keskus Autor/allikas: Ken Mürk/ERR

"How people thought at that moment, I do not know, because I was not working at RKIK then. I was a private entrepreneur, I followed this game from the media, like any ordinary citizen. What is clear to me is what is written. We have collected the materials and submitted them to court through a lawyer. I believe that the court proceedings will take place at the end of this year or the beginning of next year," Vaher said.

According to Vaher, at the moment the only option is to ask for the money back, because while in the case of procurements carried out by Estonian companies or Estonia itself one can be more flexible and make decisions independently, the use of foreign funds comes with very clear restrictions set by the European Union.

"One of the restrictions is time, and that time is up. This means that we had to carry out the procurement within a certain time. Delivery had to take place at specific times, and if that did not happen, then that was one of the reasons why we had to terminate the contract. But the most important reason was still that the goods they showed us and that we have gone to inspect with experts are simply not what Ukraine would want for winning its war," Vaher explained.

Poor-quality production artillery shells

It recently emerged that Estonia has paid a total of 70 million euros for shells intended for Ukraine that the country has not received. Due to poor‑quality production, using the shell may be dangerous or may not fulfill its purpose. In Vaher's assessment, it was not a wise decision to conclude a contract and make advance payments to a shelf company whose purpose is simply to operate in the European Union and mediate something. Upon taking office as head of RKIK, Vaher said he had no choice but to begin defending their rights.

"These contracts were already at such a stage at that moment that there was not much to do, and it was necessary to begin defending our rights. Therefore, it was clear to me in the first days that there was no escape here. Negotiations must be ended with dignity and politeness, but to defend our rights we must go to court. We worked for that, and either in March or April we began the court process," Vaher said.

Many employees who concluded the contracts at the time have since left RKIK. The same applies to the previous director general, Magnus‑Valdemar Saar.

Magnus-Valdemar Saar. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

"How they thought and what was the basis for decisions in such behavior is a matter for their conscience," Vaher said, adding that he does not know whether Saar left because of the problematic contracts.

In Vaher's assessment, the workload at RKIK was previously too large and the organization's management was different. There were too few decision‑makers, and the lack of multiple pairs of eyes could lead to mistakes. There was also no overview of why certain decisions were made and carried out at one moment or another.

Previous decisions not documented

"The National Audit Office also says today that our previous decisions at RKIK in 2024 and 2025 are not reproducible. We cannot find answers as to why we decided like this. The story that investigative journalism has unfolded — here we must say to journalists: good work — also clearly shows that our decisions and behavior are not documented. This must be done better," Vaher said.

Vaher admitted that he learned about the contracts in question on his first working day, and defense Minister Hanno Pevkur indicated that the situation must be addressed and rights defended.

"I chose the path that negotiations end and we no longer submit to these promises that yes, we will bring it soon, we are on Ukraine's side, and so on. I could do only one thing: defend our rights, because we must ensure assistance to Ukraine and the lawful use of money," the head of RKIK said.

On Tuesday, the Prosecutor's Office initiated criminal proceedings to investigate the administrative area of the Ministry of Defense, concerning circumstances addressed in both this year's and last year's National Audit Office audits. No one has been charged with a crime.

Minister of Defense Hanno Pevkur announced on Wednesday that he will resign. He had served as defense minister since 2022.

On Wednesday it emerged that Estonia sought to buy shells for Ukraine and paid a total of 70 million euros in advance to Indian businessmen who had reportedly never sold a single shell before.

World.title: Employers' leader urges Estonia to model its economic policy on the U.S.
World.content:
Estonia should look to the United States for inspiration when building its economic environment, says Ain Hanschmidt, president of the Estonian Employers' Confederation.

Employers have published their manifesto outlining what Estonia's economy should look like. One of its main recommendations for politicians is to focus on increasing productivity.

"We need more ambition. Right now, when the economy is growing, we need greater ambition. I really liked when Andrus Ansip, as prime minister, said that Estonia's goal is to reach the top five richest countries. We must have greater ambition," Hanschmidt said on an ERR television program.

Hanschmidt emphasized that to increase productivity by five to six percent annually, the economic environment must be very business‑friendly.

Calls for greater ambition

"We should take inspiration from the United States. The state of Texas has one of the best economic environments in the world. There, politicians look at things this way: if a law or regulation hinders business, they remove it or discuss how to rethink it," he said.

"The same applies to Estonia. Our economic environment must be such that all politicians, entrepreneurs, employees and officials move in step and think about how to grow the economy. Because Estonia is a democracy, some have thought that economic growth is not the most important thing — but in reality, it is the source of our standard of living," he said.

"Money doesn't make you happy — money makes you calm," Hanschmidt replied when asked how much money is needed for a good life.

He disagrees with his former colleague Janek Mäggi's claim that Estonians have become complacent.

"Estonians are very diligent workers and act thoughtfully, but sometimes the political system becomes too complicated. That's the problem," he said, recalling how many strong leaders emerged during the difficult times of the 1990s.

Stable environment key to attracting investment

He also disagrees with SEB economic analyst Mihkel Nestor, who argued that two to three percent economic growth does not make people happier.

"It does, it does," Hanschmidt insisted. "I think this dissatisfaction is our source of energy. You must criticize and be dissatisfied if you want development and want to move Estonia forward. In any case, I believe that in 2026 we will be more satisfied than five years ago, when Covid hit, the war in Ukraine began, the threats were huge and the economy was in decline. Today the economy is already growing."

A stable security environment would also bring more foreign investment, Hanschmidt added.

He said that the recent exposure of disorder in the defense sector is actually positive.

"There should be greater parliamentary or civilian oversight over those security structures that can use money. You cannot simply say it's a defense secret or a war secret," he said.

Hanschmidt sees the so‑called tax peace and the removal of the tax hump as measures that boost the economy.

End of tax hump boost consumer confidence

"People were left with significantly more money — around 800 million euros — which increased consumer confidence. Looking at card payment data, payments grew by about 12 percent. People can decide for themselves where to put their money. If we give decision‑making power only to civil servants, we have to put controls everywhere, and then things happen like 60 million disappearing somewhere in India," he said.

Regarding the wealth tax proposed by Eesti 200 chair Kristina Kallas, Hanschmidt said it is still too early.

"Sweden has a wealth tax, but they have been accumulating wealth for a long time — they haven't had a war on their territory for about 400 years. We have been diligently and smartly building our wealth since 1991. I think Estonia's economy, entrepreneurship and resources are too thin. If these are heavily taxed, the economy won't withstand it," he said.

World.title: Former EDF commander offered defense minister post
World.content:
Herem says he is weighing up the offer. Following Hanno Pevkur's resignation as defense minister on Wednesday, a replacement is being sought.

Herem said the position came up in a conversation with the prime minister outside the recording of Michal's own podcast. "Was I made an offer? Essentially, yes. But it was more an invitation to consider it, rather than, 'Hey, take the job.' I assume he has some other candidates as well. But in any case, the idea was planted in my head that I might get a phone call and then I would have to say yes or no. So now I suppose I have to think about it," Herem said.

Herem added that he will not be in Estonia next week. "I intend to carry on doing what I'm doing for now. Whatever phone call I might get, I won't be in Estonia next week," he continued.

However, Herem said he has no ambition to become a minister. "I've already contributed to developing the Estonian state, and I will continue doing so. I have to think very seriously about why I should be in that position. And why I couldn't continue doing what I'm doing today and still be useful to the country," Herem went on.

Martin Herem appearing on 'Mul pole aega,' Prime Minister Kristen Michal's own podcast. Herem said the prime minister approached him on potentially being the next defense minister outside the recording room. Source: Reform Party

"Am I ready to be a minister? No. Does Estonia need saving? Yes, it does. Do I have to do that at that level? That I'm not sure about," he added.

Speaking about the shell deal that caused the scandal, Herem defended the risks taken. "No one else is going to do these things for the Estonian state. And Estonia has helped Ukraine a great deal by taking risks. Then, at some point, when those risks materialize, you're seen as having done something wrong. I don't believe there was any corruption or anything like that," the former EDF commander said.

"And now, when you're in a situation where you see that Ukraine needs help, you think you can help, but there are certain risks involved, at some point doing nothing seems considerably worse than going ahead and perhaps getting burned. In the end, you take responsibility and resign, and that's that".

Herem, now a retired general, served as EDF commander December 2018 until June 2024. He joined private sector firm Milrem Robotics as a military strategy adviser in August last year.

Hanno Pevkur resigned as defense minister on Wednesday after a €70 million shell procurement scandal emerged. Criminal proceedings have been opened, though no one has been named as a suspect. Michal has said the Reform Party will begin discussing candidates for the new defense minister next week.

World.title: Industrial production up by 2.3% in July, led by wood and machinery
World.content:
Total industrial production rose by 2.3 percent at constant prices year‑on‑year in July, Statistics Estonia reported, with growth across all three sectors.

Output increased by 13.5 percent in mining, 16 percent in energy production and 1.1 percent in manufacturing, which had declined for five consecutive months before July.

Commenting on the results, Riin Kadarik, leading analyst at Statistics Estonia, said manufacturing was boosted by the manufacture of wood, the biggest manufacturing industry, where output increased by 10.8 percent compared with July last year. "Nearly half of the increase in output in this activity was contributed by the manufacture of solid fuels from vegetable biomass," Kadarik said.

Industrial production changes. Source: Statistics Estonia

There was also significant growth in the manufacture of machinery and equipment, where output grew by 30.3 percent, mainly due to the production of lifting equipment and special‑purpose machinery. Output increased in two‑thirds of manufacturing activities, with food production growing by 1.5 percent — its first increase since December 2025.

Of the major activities, the manufacture of fabricated metal products saw a fall in output for the second consecutive month, dropping by 0.9 percent in July.

Compared with June, seasonally adjusted total industrial production rose by 0.9 percent, with manufacturing up 0.2 percent.

In July, 65.2 percent of manufacturing production was sold to the external market. Compared with July 2025, sales of manufacturing production increased by 7.9 percent at current prices, with domestic sales up 8.6 percent and export sales up 7.5 percent.

Volume index and its trend. Source: Statistics Estonia

Energy production rose by 16 percent in July, with electricity production increasing by 9.6 percent and heat production by 13.2 percent year‑on‑year. "The increase in electricity production in July was mainly due to greater domestic production, as imports remained similar to last year's level," Kadarik said.

Statistics Estonia compiled the data on behalf of the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications.

World.title: Iraqi judiciary completes interrogation of 5,700 ISIS suspects
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Supreme Judicial Council of Iraq has officially concluded the interrogation process for 5,704 ISIS detainees who were moved from northeastern Syria earlier this year, preparing them for trial.

The First Karkh Investigation Court said in a statement on Tuesday that it concluded the investigation phase of one of Iraq’s largest terrorism-related cases in history.

The verified detainees originate from 67 different nationalities, including 3,497 Syrians and 474 Iraqis.

The courts identified very dangerous agents in key leadership, military, financial, media, and security roles inside ISIS.

Six offenders were actively linked to the captivity, detention, transfer, sale, and exploitation of Yazidi women, exposing serious international crimes.

Several suspects have previously been cleared and released due to insufficient evidence linking them to terrorism crimes.

In 2014, the terrorist group ISIS took control of large areas in Iraq and Syria before being defeated in 2017.

Over five million Iraqis had to flee the governorates of Nineveh, Salah al-Din, parts of Kirkuk, Diyala, and Anbar because of ISIS control over these areas in 2014.

Although Iraq declared in late 2017 that all of its regions were free of ISIS, the government continues to conduct security operations to hunt out any remaining members of the terrorist group.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate rises in Baghdad, remain stable in Erbil
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar against the Iraqi dinar rose on Thursday in Baghdad, the Iraqi capital, and remained stable in Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The US dollar exchange rate rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,547.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,546.5 Iraqi dinars on Thursday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad rose, ranging between 1,552.5 Iraqi dinars and 1,542.5 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate remained stable, fluctuating between 1,546 and 1,545.5 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation represented more than a 10 percent difference in exchange rates.

World.title: Iraq exports fuel oil through Jordan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The spokesperson for the Iraqi Oil Ministry, Salim al-Rikabi, told Attaqa News that Iraq began exporting fuel oil shipments via Jordan for the first time last month.

Al-Rikabi explained that Iraq is exporting fuel oil through the neighboring country, not to Jordan.

The Iraqi official did not disclose the details of the agreement, its duration, or when it came into effect.

Iraqi oil shipments started flowing to Jordan in early August through the Trebil border crossing, the only land border crossing between the two countries, at a rate of 10,000 barrels per day, which were stored in the facilities of the Jordan Oil Terminals Company (JOTC), Jordan’s state-owned petroleum logistics and independent storage provider.

Through Jordan, a shipment totaling 307,000 barrels was exported to Greece.

Following the Strait of Hormuz crisis, which began with the United States’ war against Iran on February 28, Iraqi fuel oil shipments began transiting through Syria via tanker trucks, with storage at the Baniyas refinery before shipping to worldwide markets.

Between March and the end of August, Iraq exported 21.4 million barrels of fuel oil through Syria and only 307,000 barrels through Jordan.

Iraqi fuel oil exports started to increase following the Middle East conflict until the end of August in an attempt to compensate for the declining supplies via the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: 38 officers, 3,000 personnel dismissed over corruption in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Interior announced on Thursday that it permanently dismissed 38 officers and 180 personnel over administrative and financial corruption, with another 3,245 personnel discharged for desertion.

The purge represents a significant internal effort as part of the ongoing “Operation Dawn,” a nationwide anti-corruption campaign spearheaded by Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s government. The campaign has targeted numerous public officials and high-profile individuals.

According to an official statement from Miqdad Miri, the spokesperson for the Interior Ministry, the total number of individuals affected encompasses various categories of misconduct.

After receiving clear evidence of their direct involvement in bribery and financial misconduct, 38 officers were permanently removed from service.

Finalized judicial verdicts convicting 180 enlisted personnel of corruption accusations resulted in their official removal from service.

As part of larger ministry attempts to reestablish strong institutional discipline, 3,245 service personnel were discharged only for abandoning their duties.

These dismissals took place within the first 100 days of the current government’s tenure.

This security-sector cleanup is part of the larger nationwide drive “Operation Dawn.” Between late June and August, security operations resulted in the arrest of at least 210 lawmakers, public servants, and business executives.

World.title: Iraq, AIIB discuss financing development projects
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Finance Minister Faleh Sari met with a delegation from the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) led by Konstantin Limitovskiy on Wednesday to discuss funding infrastructure and development projects in Iraq.

During their meeting in Baghdad, the AIIB delegation reviewed its global and regional portfolios to outline how its framework will apply to Iraq across the transportation, energy, water, and digital infrastructure sectors, according to a statement cited by the Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The discussions focused on the Development Road Project, Iraq’s mega-highway and rail corridor intended to connect the Gulf to Europe.

The AIIB publicly stated its willingness to fund and assist this important trans-regional corridor, acknowledging its enormous potential to drive economic diversification.

The Iraqi Ministry of Transport held separate discussions with the World Bank and the AIIB to determine the technological integrations necessary for the project’s ports and rail networks.

The AIIB delegation expressed its willingness to assist and fund important projects in Iraq, particularly major infrastructure projects, such as the Development Road project, which would boost the country’s economic development.

World.title: Iraq launches plan to recover 100,000 artifacts smuggled abroad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has launched a comprehensive plan to recover over 100,000 artifacts that were unearthed through illegal excavation and smuggled out of the country.

The Iraqi Ministry of Culture, Tourism, and Antiquities announced a broad endeavor to recover the country’s stolen Mesopotamian heritage using a combination of cultural diplomacy, security surveillance, and strong legal action.

The ministry’s undersecretary, Qasim al-Sudani, told the Iraqi News Agency (INA) that the government’s agenda prioritizes the tourism sector.

The strategy emphasizes recovering documented items that were assigned official museum inventory numbers prior to their theft and smuggling, especially during the tumultuous period following the 2003 US-led invasion.

The initiative also seeks to tackle the significant number of unrecorded artifacts found during illegal and random excavations.

Since these items lack formal records, they pose a substantially more difficult legal issue to monitor and authenticate.

The Iraqi government has formed a combined domestic task force comprising the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ministry of Interior, the National Intelligence Service, and the National Security Service to carry out the plan.

Security agencies are cooperating with Iraqi embassies to identify stolen treasures that appear at public or private auctions abroad.

While countries like the United Kingdom and the United States have actively assisted in the return of tens of thousands of artifacts, Iraqi officials have indicated that some nations have intentionally delayed the repatriation process.

Iraq is also taking legal actions internationally against foreign businesses or individuals who are keeping Iraqi artifacts.

World.title: Iraq evaluates exploration blocks to optimize gas output
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Oil is actively assessing its exploration blocks and foreign alliances to maximize domestic gas output.

Director of the state-owned Midland Oil Company (MOC), Mohammed Yassin Hassan, told the Iraqi News Agency (INA) that the ministry is focusing on unexploited exploration areas rather than existing resources.

The strategic measure seeks to attract multinational corporations to invest in Iraq’s growing natural gas sector.

Instead of altering production at current sites, the Oil Ministry is focusing on new exploration regions to identify new deposits.

Due to the strong interest in Iraq’s untapped energy potential, multinational energy businesses have already begun contacting the ministry.

Iraq’s MOC is actively pursuing partnerships with major US firms, such as ConocoPhillips, to lead gas development projects in important areas in the provinces of Diyala and Anbar.

Expanding operations in blocks such as the Akkas and Mansuriya gas fields is critical to Iraq’s long-term strategy for achieving energy independence and providing the necessary fuel for power plants to generate electricity.

World.title: Marsoumi: Iraq’s 10M bpd oil goal faces $75B cost and OPEC+ hurdles
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq’s strategic plan to scale crude oil production to 10 million barrels per day (bpd) by 2030 faces formidable structural, financial, and geopolitical hurdles, prominent Iraqi economic analyst Dr. Nabil Al-Marsoumi warned on Wednesday, September 2, 2026.

The assessment follows directives issued on Tuesday by Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi, who instructed the Ministry of Oil to expand exploration licensing rounds and ramp up extraction across fields in federal territory and the Kurdistan Region to target nearly 10 million bpd over the next four years.

Al-Marsoumi outlined four primary structural constraints standing between Iraq’s current production baseline and the 10-million-bpd horizon:

OPEC+ Baseline & Quota Negotiation: Iraq currently produces approximately 4.431 million bpd against an OPEC+ baseline allocation of 4.651 million bpd. Pushing production toward 10 million bpd requires formal revision of Iraq’s sovereign quota—a concession requiring consensus among major OPEC+ members.

Sustainable Capacity Ceiling: US petroleum consultancy DeGolyer and MacNaughton is actively auditing the maximum sustainable capacity across 19 OPEC+ nations. Preliminary assessments project Iraq’s sustainable 12-month ceiling at 5.0 to 5.5 million bpd, revealing a 4.5-million-bpd capacity deficit below the 2030 target.

Capital Expenditure Threshold ($75 Billion): Based on global industry benchmarks averaging $15 billion in capital investment per 1 million bpd of added capacity, Iraq must mobilize roughly $75 billion in upstream and midstream funding. This capital must finance seawater treatment and injection facilities, storage farm expansions, pumping stations, and new maritime and northern pipeline export corridors.

Price Collapse & Market Saturation Risks: Global oil absorption capacity remains constrained by demand growth projections. Injecting millions of additional Iraqi barrels risks igniting a market-share price war among producers, which could trigger a global oil price collapse harmful to Baghdad’s hydrocarbon-dependent treasury.

Comparative Analysis: Current Capacity vs. 2030 Target

Metric / Parameter Current Level (2026) 2030 Government Target Gap / Required Expansion Crude Output ~4.431 Million bpd 10.000 Million bpd +5.569 Million bpd Sustainable Ceiling 5.0 – 5.5 Million bpd 10.000 Million bpd +4.500 Million bpd OPEC+ Production Baseline 4.651 Million bpd Revised Allocation Required Requires OPEC+ Consensus Estimated Capital Outlay Baseline operational budget ~$75 Billion cumulative $15B per 1M bpd capacity Export Infrastructure Constrained southern/northern routes New northern & deepwater sea lines Major pipeline & storage expansion

Al-Marsoumi cautioned that upstream expansion cannot occur in isolation from global energy market fundamentals. Without substantial foreign direct investment to finance water injection schemes and deepwater export berths, aggressive target-setting risks outpacing actual midstream logistics.

Furthermore, aggressively pursuing volume over price discipline could depress international crude benchmarks, reducing net state oil revenues even as export volumes increase.

World.title: Punjab government to hike DA of 85,000 employees from 42 to 60 pc: Minister Aman Arora
World.content:
Punjab government will raise the Dearness Allowance of around 85,000 government employees

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Chandigarh, Punjab government will raise the Dearness Allowance of around 85,000 government employees recruited after July 17, 2020 by 18 per cent to 60 per cent, Cabinet Minister Aman Arora said on Friday.Speaking to mediapersons here, Arora said a recommendation in this regard was made by the Cabinet Sub-Committee formed to examine the issues of employees.The announcement is significant as employees recruited after July 17, 2020 were getting a pay equivalent to the Central pay scales, along with 42 per cent Dearness Allowance (DA). These were much lower than the pay scales of employees recruited before July 2020, who were paid as per the Punjab Pay Commission.Arora said there were two pay scales in Punjab, which was leading to conflicting interests and confusion: the Punjab basic pay scales and the one equivalent to the Central basic pay scales (as per the 7th Central Pay Commission)."Punjab basic pay scales, which traditionally are higher, range from 30 to 70 per cent more than the Central basic pay. And when DA is added to it, which is currently 42 per cent, the salary increases much above the Central pay scales," he said."When we calculate and compare, even with 60 per cent DA added to Central basic pay, the Punjab pay scales and take-home salaries are higher," he said.Arora said the previous Congress government had decided to hire employees on the Central pay scales after July 17, 2020.In the last six years, 85,000 employees have been recruited.The Mann government will give them a "Janmashtami gift" as the three-member Cabinet Sub-Committee has decided that the DA of these employees will be raised from 42 to 60 per cent. The committee's recommendation will be sent to the chief minister, Arora said.He, however, said that this hike will not benefit employees recruited before July 2020."From day one, the Bhagwant Mann government has been talking about the welfare of every section. We cannot imagine good governance without our employees," he said.The development comes amid over 3 lakh government employees, who went on a statewide strike on August 27, pressing the state government to accept their various demands, including the release of their pending 18 per cent DA.They have also threatened to go on mass casual leave on September 8 if the state government does not withdraw a recent notice imposing disciplinary action against those who remained on "unauthorised absence" on August 27.The employees have given the state government time till September 7 to withdraw the notice issued to protesting employees.Punjab government on Thursday appealed to employee unions to engage with it through dialogue rather than confrontation, calling employees the backbone of good governance.

World.title: SC overturns trial court, HC orders to acquit kidnap-murder accused
World.content:
Supreme Court freed a man sentenced by lower courts

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: For the third time this week, Supreme Court freed a man sentenced by lower courts - in a kidnapping and murder case in the latest instance - questioning their analysis of evidence, and flagging loopholes in the prosecution theory tying the accused to the crime, reports Dhananjay Mahapatra.A man was kidnapped in Telangana in 2012 and his father paid a ransom of Rs 1.5 lakh against a demand of Rs 23 lakh. His body was recovered from a fridge in a flat based on the disclosure of the accused, one of whom died during pendency of trial. A trial court convicted the five other accused. Telangana HC analysed evidence and acquitted four, but convicted one.The Supreme Court said barring the postmortem report indicating strangulation, and finding of the body, there was no substantive evidence to link the accused to the murder.Setting aside conviction and sentence, a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said, âThat victim died of âasphyxia due to smothering, associated with strangulationâ, is established by the autopsy report and the dead body was detected, tucked away in a refrigerator inside an apartment. But for these, there is no scrap of evidence, worthy of reliance, to connect the six accused to the murder or even the flat.âIn another case, a man was accused of luring a boy with snacks to sodomise him. He was convicted by an Ambala court in April 2010 for the March 2007 âcrimeâ of unnatural sex and murder, and given life term. Punjab and Haryana HC in Oct 2022 dismissed the appeal.A bench of Justices Sanjay Kumar and Sanjeev Sachdeva said police failed to conduct DNA test of the semen in the undergarment of the accused to match it with the rectal swab collected from victimâs undergarment. SC said the âlast seen withâ theory is doubtful and that there were several missing links in the chain of the prosecution case. It acquitted the man, who had served 17 years in prison. The drawing of judicial curtains on the case had unpleasant outcomes: a man lost his young child to a crime which went unpunished, while a man unfairly convicted lost his prime years.In the third case, a murder in Bihar 25 years ago saw a trial court and Patna HC convict six persons. A bench of Justices Pardiwala and Chandran acquitted the convicts saying, âThere is complete lack of evidence, and eyewitnesses testimonies do not inspire confidenceâ¦ The case is not that of faulty investigation but of no probe having been carried out.

World.title: 'Exceptionally rare': All 3 hydraulic systems of plane failed together
World.content:
MUMBAI: Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau's preliminary report has confirmed what pilots and engineers call an exceptionally rare event, the near-simultaneous loss of all three hydraulic systems on the A320neo aircraft at 36,000 feet.

Hydraulic systems are the fluid-pressure circuits that physically move an aircraft's wing and tail surfaces. The green, blue and yellow systems dropped out within seconds of each other, triggering an autopilot disengagement, a stall warning and a brief altitude upset that injured 24 flyers.

The accident occurred when the eight-year-old A320neo (VT-EXO) carrying 145 people had just been cleared to climb from 34,000 feet to 36,000 feet after entering the airspace controlled by Kolkata ATC.

At 9:32:43am IST, within four seconds the flight control system detected loss of all the three hydraulic systems.

âTriple hydraulic failure close to unthinkableâ

In the next few seconds, the autopilot disengaged, a continuous repetitive chime sounded, and the stall warning triggered for two seconds. âThe aircraft encountered altitude upset. Initially, it gained 372 ft and fell by 292 ft from its assigned 36,000 feet flight level during the event,â the report said.





It did not give information on the cause of the triple hydraulic failure, nor did it put forth any safety recommendations for the A320 aircraft type. It said the investigation is in progress and hydraulic components, fluid samples and recorder data have been collected and are still being analysed.

The critical information on the probable cause and contributory factors is likely to be released in the final report, expected to be published on or before Aug 4, 2027.

In simple terms, hydraulic pressure is what physically moves an aircraftâs control surfaces, the ailerons on the wings that make it roll, the elevators on the tail that make it pitch up or down, and the rudder that makes it yaw left or right. Pilots move the stick and pedals, but it is hydraulic power that pushes the actual surfaces. An A320 carries three independent hydraulic circuits so that losing one, or even two, still leaves enough pressure to fly and manoeuvre the aircraft normally.

âLosing all three at once is considered close to unthinkable, because the A320 has a triple-redundant hydraulic design which ensures no combination of failures can disable flight controls entirely. It is the kind of failure engineers cite alongside a handful of decades-old incidents involving other aircraft types, none of them an A320,â said a senior aircraft maintenance engineer. The notable total hydraulic loss events that occurred globally are the 1985 JAL 123 (Boeing 747), the 1989 United Airlines DC-10, and a DHL A300 that was hit by a missile over Baghdad in 2003.

Following the triple hydraulic failure, the co-pilot, who was flying the aircraft, responded first to the upset before the captain took over the controls. Recovery was swift, the blue system came back within seconds, followed shortly by yellow and green, restoring normal flight control surfaces, the report said.

World.title: Hours after AAIB report, AI sacks Phuket flight pilot
World.content:
Air India Friday sacked the pilot-in-command of its badly rattled Aug 4 Phuket-Delhi

Software malfunction or manual intervention? Final report may reveal

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Air India Friday sacked the pilot-in-command of its badly rattled Aug 4 Phuket-Delhi flight hours after Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau's preliminary report concluded the "PIC was found non-negative for psycho-active substance in the confirmatory (dope) test". Terming this confirmation a "serious concern", AAIB has asked Directorate General of Civil Aviation to "take appropriate actions as deemed fit to prevent abuse of psychoactive substance" on "priority" in its interim safety recommendations and conclusion. Aviation secretary Samir Sinha had soon after this accident asked DGCA chief Vir Vikram Yadav to make dope rules more stringent.AI was considering action, including termination, against the PIC for some weeks now but was awaiting AAIB's prelim report into what has now been categorised as an "accident" due to its severity and impact. An AI spokesperson said: "Safety remains AI's highest priority. In line with AI's zero-tolerance approach to violation of safety, fitness or regulatory requirements, the pilot's employment has been terminated with immediate effect. "When the badly rattled Airbus A320 had landed in Delhi with 24 injured people and a damaged aircraft cabin, both the pilots were subjected to post-flight breath-analyser examination as per standard protocol.They cleared that test.But for some reason which may be disclosed in the final report, the unusual step of conducting dope tests was taken in this case. âThe sample of PIC was found non-negative. Blood samples of both the flight crew were sent to path lab for confirmatory (dope) test. The confirmatory test report of PIC was found non-negative whereas the sample of co-pilot was found negative in both the tests,â stated the interim report.An AAIB probe is on to find what caused the Airbus A320 to suffer an extremely rare failure of all three hydraulic systems within seconds. The final report is expected to reveal whether it happened due to something going wrong with the aircraftâs hardware or software or whether due to some manual intervention with the PIC having some role in that, if any. Hydraulics on an Airbus A320 use pressurised liquid to move heavy flight controls, lower the landing gear, and stop the wheels.Such was the impact of this âeventâ which happened that 24 people got injured and the aircraft cabin saw significant damage, including a lavatory commode getting uprooted from its location. The overhead ceiling panel was found cracked or deformed at various places. Most of the passenger service unit panels were found dislocated or bent at various places. The overhead handrail was found broken and sealing panel found dislocated near the tenth row. The forward right side emergency exit handle was found broken.The cabin supervisor (head cabin crew) apprised the cockpit about the injuries suffered by the passengers and crew. The crew assessed the cabin situation and took the decision of continuing the flight to its destination Delhi and not diverting to the nearest en route airport.Following the report, AI said: âWe acknowledge the release of the preliminary report by the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau and continue to extend our full cooperation to the investigation, including providing access to all relevant operational, maintenance and technical records. Safety remains Air Indiaâs highest priority. Our pilots undergo rigorous training, regular proficiency checks, medical examinations and other regulatory assessments in accordance with applicable national and international requirements. Following the incident, Air India has started voluntary testing of 100% of its pilots as a further step to reinforce its safety-first approach.â âThe airline maintains zero tolerance for any breach of safety, fitness or regulatory requirements,â Air Indiaâs statement added.

World.title: Europe waking up to Modi's warning 'a bit late': Belgian PM
World.content:
Belgian PM said India and Europe were now facing similar challenges

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI/MUMBAI: Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever on Friday said Europe had been slow to recognise the risks of becoming too dependent on other economies, admitting that Indian PM Narendra Modi had warned it about the problem much earlier but was not heard.De Wever, who was on a two-day visit to India to strengthen ties in trade, investment, technology and strategic cooperation, said India and Europe were now facing similar challenges as economic dependencies were increasingly being used as leverage. "We do not like dependencies becoming weaponised against us. You have lived this history. Your Prime Minister warned Europe about this long time ago already. But he was ignored. He wasn't listened to. We are listening now," De Wever said at a Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) event.Calling Europe's awakening "a bit late", De Wever said the region was now having the "right debates" about who it could work with in a world where major economic powers were moving in different directions.He said India was the most important partner for Europe among countries that believed in multilateralism and cooperation based on "respect and not force"."If India is not on the list, then you have missed something fundamental. India is on that list. It's number one," De Wever said.In an apparent reference to China, De Wever said Europe was seeking to reduce its dependence on "big economical powerhouses" that were moving away from rules-based cooperation. "I will not name them China," he said, adding that such a direction was not what Europe wanted.Speaking on the occasion, Union commerce minister Piyush Goyal said the India-EU FTA was a win-win for everyone. "It will open opportunities for farmers, start ups, women entrepreneurs, it has something for everyone. It's been deftly negotiated protecting sensitive sectors on both sides. It offers huge potential for both sides," he said.

World.title: Coal stock at thermal plants plummets, 'critical' at 50 units
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Coal stocks at thermal power plants across the country have fallen to less than half the recommended level, with 50 plants classified as having 'critically low' inventories as on Sept 2 amid high electricity demand and monsoon-led disruptions in supplies, Central Electricity Authority data showed.

The plants, with a combined capacity of around 224 GW, had 28.2 million tonnes (MT) of coal as of Wednesday, 48% of the prescribed requirement of 58.7 MT. The available stock is equivalent to about nine days of coal requirement at 85% plant load factor, against the normal requirement of around 19 days.

The plants classified as short on coal stocks have less than 25% of their normative inventories. Coal ministry officials, however, said all critical plants were being monitored by an inter-ministerial team of officials on a day-to-day basis and regular fuel supplies were being provided to them.

Of the 50 plants, 45 are based on domestic fuel, four are designed for imported coal and one runs on washery rejects.

A senior coal ministry official said, "Classification of a thermal power plant as critical is a routine monitoring parameter under norms laid down by CEA. It simply means closer tracking and priority action. These plants are not running out of supply."

Though the normative coal requirement at power plants is calculated at 3.1 MT every day at 85% plant load factor, officials said the actual requirement is around 2.4 MT.





The monsoon sees supply disruptions every year. The situation starts improving from Sept onwards as rains begin to recede.

While the power ministry did not respond to requests for a reaction, sources said some coal-fired plants had been asked to defer scheduled maintenance to ensure continuity of electricity generation.

World.title: SC awards pension to Mumbai engineer who forged ST certificate
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

has rewarded a wrongdoer - a man who got appointed as a junior civil engineer in Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai (MCGM) by producing a forged ST certificate, and, subsequently, stalled the scrutiny of his eligibility for quota for more than a decade - by allowing him to superannuate in peace with retirement benefits.

Shirish P Patil got a certificate in 1984 by identifying himself as belonging to the 'Tokre Koli' Scheduled Tribe community. Based on the certificate, he was appointed a junior civil engineer in MCGM in 1994. He misplaced the original ST certificate but managed to secure a fresh one from the sub-divisional magistrate, Bhusawal division, in Oct 2000.

Following scrutiny initiated by MCGM, the Police Vigilance Cell traced Patil's family history and found that his ancestors had been recorded as 'Koli', 'Hindu Koli' and 'Hindu Suryawanshi Koli', none of which belonged to the ST category.

In July 2009, MCGM issued a show cause notice to Patil.

He successfully dodged and delayed proceedings before the scrutiny committee until Jan 2020, when the panel rejected his plea that his lawyer and elderly family members were not available, and invalidated the ST certificate. HC dismissed his appeal against cancellation of ST status.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

SC, however, stayed Patil's dismissal from service through an interim order on Nov 18, 2021.





As a result, the engineer continued to serve until June 30, 2025, when he retired after being employed with MCGM for more than three decades based on a forged ST certificate.

A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi Thursday upheld the cancellation of Patil's ST certificate and Bombay HC order. However, it took a lenient view given his undertaking that he or any of his family members "shall (not) be entitled to claim any future benefit on the basis of the invalidated ST certificate".

The ruling contrasts with SC's consistent rulings against benefits accruing to people who forge SC or ST certificates to gain admission or employment.

World.title: CPI(ML)L to launch ‘Fix the schools’ campaign, seeks to keep Jantar Mantar momentum going
World.content:
CPI(ML) Liberation is looking to build on the gains made by its studentsâ wing AISA

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Preparing to assert the Leftâs presence in upcoming state polls next year in Punjab, UP and Uttarakhand where it proposes to field candidates in certain constituencies, the CPI(ML) Liberation is looking to build on the gains made by its studentsâ wing AISA with Gen Z during the recent Jantar Mantar protests by launching a nationwide outreach âSchool theek karo, shiksha sudharoâ (Fix the schools, improve education) to focus on educational reform from primary to higher education levels.Focusing on educational reform from primary to higher education levels, the campaign, that also seeks to reach out to Gen Alpha, will be rolled out on Teachers Day on Saturday. Parallelly a series of public meetings will be held on studentsâ issues starting with a public meeting on Sunday in Patna. Youth, teachers, parents, civil society and concerned citizens are expected to come together in large numbers at the CPI(ML)L event to share their experiences on education ranging from the National Education policy to the examination system and paper leaks.CPI(ML)L general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya and AISA president Neha Bora will be present at the Patna meeting. The Left party also plans to reinforce its demand for bringing down the age of voting from 18 to 16 citing the increasing awareness and assertiveness of boys and girls in this age group, a reflection of which was evident in the recent student protests. Similar meetings will follow in Uttar Pradesh in Lucknow, Varanasi, Rae Bareli, Meerut, Allahabad, Gorakhpur, Azamgarh and Faizabad between September 9 and 18.âThe Gen Z protests brought into focus the examination system and now we want to retain the momentum created by expanding the outreach. The âschool theek karo, shiksha sudharoâ outreach will be a citizens campaign to convey to authorities by way of petitions and agitations at the grassroots level to demand quality education,â Bhattacharya said.With 2027 set to see states like UP going to polls, Bhattacharya said that the CPI(ML)L proposes to contest elections in Punjab by fielding candidates on seats where they have a grassroots presence largely in the Malwa region and also contest from some constituencies in UP and Uttarakhand either as a larger Left bloc if an alliance with other parties works out or else on its own.As part of the mobilisation, the CPI(ML)L will also be holding a major farmers conference on September 20-21 in Punjab to raise key concerns affecting agriculture, labour including the impact of the Indo-US trade deal on the sector.

World.title: Trump calls Iran conflict 'small potatoes', says he agrees with Vance that it's not 'war'
World.content:
U.S. President Donald Trump on Friday (September 4, 2026) said the conflict in Iran is “small potatoes” as he defended Vice President JD Vance for asserting that months of on-and-off attacks in West Asia are not a “war.”

Asked during an Oval Office exchange about Mr. Vance's comments made a day earlier, Mr. Trump noted that U.S. strikes on Iran are now “intermittent” and seemed to downplay the intensity of a war that's cost U.S. taxpayers more than $37.5 billion and left 18 U.S. service members dead.

“I can understand what he's saying,” said Mr. Trump. He added, “I call it a military conflict because it's small potatoes for us. It's not a big thing." Mr. Vance on Thursday (September 3), during a White House press briefing, rejected the use of the word “war” to describe the US fighting with Iran and steered clear of predicting that the 6-month-old conflict would be over by November's midterm elections, in which Republicans are trying to hang on to their narrow majorities in Congress.

“I wouldn't call it a war,” Mr. Vance said after being asked during a White House press briefing about whether the fighting could end before voters cast their ballots in the November 3 congressional elections. “Right now, there is no active shooting.” Vance's assertion came even as Iran fired at U.S. Gulf ally Kuwait on Thursday in retaliation for rounds of US strikes on Iran earlier in the week.

Mr. Trump, in Friday's exchange with reporters, added that the US death toll in the Iran conflict is relatively lower than in some other recent U.S. wars. The U.S., along with Israel, have only carried out air strikes in the Iran war, which began on February 28, and has not deployed troops into the country.

“We did Venezuela and we did this. In Venezuela, we lost nobody,” said Trump, referring to the January US military operation to seize former Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro and spirit him to New York City to face federal drug trafficking charges.

“And this, we lost 18 people. And, in Vietnam we lost 100,000 people. And in other conflicts, we lost tens of thousands of people.” A total of 58,220 members of the US armed forces died during the Vietnam War, according to records from the U.S. National Archives.

Pressed by a reporter on describing the conflict as “small potatoes" when 18 U.S. service members have been killed, Trump responded by reiterating his argument that the conflict—one that he said at the outset of the war would last a matter of weeks—has led to the defanging of Iran's nuclear program.

“Iran will not have a nuclear weapon because if they did you probably wouldn't be standing here,” Mr. Trump said.

World.title: Sree Krishna Jayanti processions part of RSS’ political project: Jayarajan
World.content:
Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] leader P. Jayarajan has alleged that Sree Krishna Jayanti processions in Keralam are part of an “RSS political project” aimed at expanding its influence among families in the State.

Mr. Jayarajan said processions marking ‘Chathaya Dinam’, the birth anniversary of social reformer Sree Narayana Guru, were the only such processions seen on the streets of Keralam earlier.

He alleged that Sree Krishna Jayanti celebrations were subsequently introduced as part of the RSS’ efforts to build a political base among families. He was speaking in a recent podcast series of the CPI(M)’s Kannur district committee.

“Faith in Lord Krishna has existed in Keralam for a long time, but people belonging to the lower castes were not allowed entry into Sree Krishna temples. This continued until the Temple Entry Proclamation,” Mr. Jayarajan said, adding that even members of the Nair community faced restrictions on temple entry, as pointed out by social reformer Mannath Padmanabhan.

It was in this context that Sree Krishna Jayanti processions should be viewed as an RSS political project, he claimed.

World.title: Probe on into spotting of fake note bundle at Thoppumpady
World.content:
The Thoppumpady police have launched a probe after recovering 106 counterfeit Indian currency notes of ₹500 denomination from near a bar at Thoppumpady in Kochi.

The bundle of notes was found in an abandoned black pouch by a local resident on Thursday night. The man alerted the police who in turn confirmed that the notes were fake.

The police registered a case on Friday and have started examining CCTV footage from the area and nearby locations.

A detailed investigation is on to determine whether the counterfeit notes were intended for circulation, the police said.

World.title: Former Deputy Collector held in bribery case in Keralam’s Kochi
World.content:
The Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB) on Friday arrested a retired Deputy Collector in connection with a bribery case in which three people, including a tahsildar, were apprehended on August 13. Kripa N.K., 59, a resident of Kadavanthra here, was arrested for allegedly playing a middleman in the ₹10 lakh bribery case, the VACB said.

The VACB zeroed in on Mr. Kripa while probing the case in which Kanayannur tahsildar (land records) Jose Antony Hartis and two alleged agents—Rajesh N.S., 49, of Kadavanthra and Jose Shibyin, 44, of Vyttila— were arrested for allegedly demanding ₹10 lakh from a man from Kaloor.

The money was allegedly sought for settling a complaint against the man’s property and facilitating its conversion from ‘nilam’ (paddy land) in revenue records. The alleged agents were reportedly caught accepting ₹2 lakh in cash and ₹8 lakh through a cheque, while the tahsildar was subsequently arrested in the operation.

World.title: 24 injured as bus rams toll plaza pillar at Kumbalam
World.content:
Twenty-four people were injured after a private bus they were travelling in rammed a pillar of the Kumbalam toll plaza on Friday morning. The accident took place around 8 a.m. as the bus, which was on its way to Kaloor from Eramalloor, reportedly lost control.

The injured were rushed to a nearby private hospital and given emergency care.

The toll plaza pillar was damaged in the impact of the accident, and vehicle movement through one of the lanes was affected.

The Panangad police registered a case.

World.title: Tenure of TDB Chief Vigilance and Security Officer extended until January 2027, State informs Kerala High Court
World.content:
The State government has informed the Kerala High Court that the tenure of the Chief Vigilance Officer of the Travancore Devaswom Board (TDB) has been extended till January 31, 2027.

A Division Bench of Justice V. Raja Vijayaraghavan and K.V. Jayakumar directed the State to extend the tenure of two civil police officers assisting the Chief Vigilance and Security Officer and fill up the existing vacancy of one sub-inspector on deputation basis.

The court instructed the State to act expeditiously on the matter considering the Vigilance wing’s significant role in maintaining transparency and ensuring effective supervision at the Sabarimala Sannidhanam.

World.title: West Bengal fire department orders vacating the basement and two floors of Abhishek’s office
World.content:
The controversy over the office of Trinamool Congress leader Abhishek Banerjee at Camac Street is refusing to die down. A day after the office of the Diamond Harbour MP was vandalised by miscreants, the West Bengal Fire Department on Friday (September 4, 2026) ordered that the basement and two floors of a high-rise building be vacated.

“Be it pertinent to mention that Renewal of Fire Safety Certificate (RFSC) for occupancy of the 2B+G+7-storied Business Building at premises no. 9, Abanindranath Tagore Sarani (Camac Street). Kolkata-700017, bearing memo no: IND/FES/20182019/1/37021, dated 10.08.2023, was valid for three years which has expired. In the said RFSC, it was clearly recommended to renew the same before expiry. However, you failed to do so,” the order by the State Fire Department said. The order directed that the said occupancy until and unless the fire safety measures are complied and the RFSC was obtained.

Copies of the order have been sent to the Kolkata Municipal Corporation, the officer-in-charge of Shakespeare Sarani Police Station and the CESC for necessary action. A joint team of police and fire officials conducted a floor-by-floor inspection of fire safety measures in the building on Monday. On Thursday, the premises were vandalised, and six people were arrested for the violence.

The premises at 9 Camac Street in Kolkata have been used by Abhishek Banerjee over the past several years. Personnel from Kolkata Police and senior Trinamool Congress leaders were embroiled in a scuffle on August 27 over the removal of a party hoarding on the building.

The police have registered FIRs and questioned Trinamool leaders in connection with the incident. Abhishek Banerjee and Rajya Sabha MP Derek O’ Brien were also summoned by Kolkata Police in connection with the incident.

After the defeat of the Trinamool Congress in the West Bengal Assembly elections in 2026, the office of Abhishek Banerjee at Amtala in his constituency has also been targeted. The Calcutta High Court had ordered a status quo on attempts by the administration to demolish the office of the Trinamool leader at Amtala.

The Trinamool Congress leadership, including former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee and Abhishek Banerjee, had described these attempts to attack, demolish and vacate party offices as “political vendetta” by the Bharatiya Janata Party government.

World.title: India in continuous touch with Ukraine and Russia to help end the conflict: Jaishankar
World.content:
India has been in continuous touch with both the Ukrainian and Russian sides and is trying to see if there are ideas and suggestions which can be developed in some way that will contribute to the mitigation or the cessation of the conflict, External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar said on Friday (September 4, 2026).

Mr. Jaishankar, who arrived in Warsaw from Kyiv, where he held talks with top Ukrainian leadership on Thursday (September 3), made the remarks after he met Poland's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski.

Addressing a joint press meet alongside Sikorski, Jaishankar said that he discussed the complex global challenges, including supply chain resilience and food, fuel and fertiliser security, with his Polish counterpart.

"The Deputy Prime Minister and I also understandably discussed some major global and regional issues, notable among them is the war in Ukraine, now in its fifth year... I myself have just come here from Kyiv," he said, referring to his visit to Ukraine a day earlier.

Replying to a question, he said India has been in continuous touch with both the Ukrainian and Russian sides.

"What we are trying to do is to see if there are ideas and suggestions which can be developed in some way in which they will contribute to the mitigation, ideally, the cessation of the conflict," he added.

A day earlier, Mr. Jaishankar had said in Ukraine that India is ready to extend "any help in any manner" to end the Ukraine-Russia war.

He had met President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and his Ukrainian counterpart Andrii Sybiha in Kyiv on Thursday.

After talks with EAM Jaishankar, Mr. Zelenskyy said that he was "grateful to India for its commitment to ending this unjust war." "This certainly must not be a time of war. Peace is needed. This is India’s clear position," he said and hoped that other major world powers would also take a clear stance that this war must end and that a reliable peace must be achieved.

On Friday, Mr. Jaishankar reiterated that India believes that endless war must give way to an end to war.

"These are wars without winners. Every additional day means more death, more destruction, more loss to the parties themselves, and more cost to the rest of the world," he said in Warsaw.

He recalled that this concern was voiced publicly by Prime Minister Narendra Modi recently.

"Our efforts must therefore focus on promoting dialogue and diplomacy. We must each do what we can in whichever way we believe could be most effective and support the efforts of others to bring this conflict to an end. This is India's strong conviction, and we are acting on it," he added. On India's purchases of Russian oil, the minister said the issue is a conflict, and its solution lies in negotiations, not in trade.

"This war is not going to end... not because somebody chose to buy or not buy oil or alumina or fertilisers or metals and minerals. It will end when there is diplomacy, when there is dialogue and when there is negotiation. So, I think let's diagnose the problem right," he said while replying to another question.

World.title: Security forces kill 48 terrorists in 'high-tempo' Balochistan operations over 72 hours: ISPR
World.content:
Security forces have killed 48 terrorists in multiple “high-tempo” anti-terror operations across Balochistan over the past three days, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said on Friday.

According to the military’s media wing, the operations were carried out in Mastung, Quetta, Kalat and Sibi districts against “Indian proxies, Fitna-al-Hindustan and Fitna-al-Khawarij”.

The state uses the term Fitna-al-Khawarij for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and has designated Balochistan-based groups as Fitna-al-Hindustan to highlight India’s alleged role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan.

In an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in Mastung district on Friday, security forces identified the movement of terrorists and engaged them. Six “Indian-sponsored terrorists” were killed in the ensuing exchange of fire, the ISPR said.

A cache of ammunition and improvised explosive devices (IEDs) was also recovered and destroyed during the operation, it added.

In another IBO in the Shaban area of Quetta district, security forces identified “four khawarij hideouts”. Following an exchange of fire, 26 terrorists were killed, according to the ISPR.

In Kalat district, security forces raided a terrorist hideout, killing two terrorists in the ensuing firefight, the military said.

Meanwhile, in the Bhag area of Sibi district, security forces foiled an attempt by terrorists to raid a local police station. Two terrorists were killed in the operation, according to the ISPR.

“In last 48-72 hours, 48 terrorists belonging to Indian proxy, Fitna-al-Hindustan and Fitna-al-Khawarij have been neutralised across Balochistan,” the ISPR said.

Earlier today, ISPR issued a statement regarding a September 2 IBO in Kalat district, where 12 terrorists were killed. The IBO was conducted on the reported presence of terrorists belonging to the Indian proxy Fitna-al-Hindustan, the military’s media wing said.

President Asif Ali Zardari hailed the professional capabilities of the security forces for eliminating the terrorists in operations across Balochistan.

“The killing of more than 1,188 terrorists in Balochistan this year alone is evidence of the threats facing Pakistan and the readiness of the security forces,” he said in a statement.

The president expressed the government’s firm resolve to eradicate “foreign-backed and enabled terrorism” from the country.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi also commended the security forces for the series of operations that resulted in the killing of 36 terrorists, APP reported.

In a statement, Naqvi said their elimination reflected the forces’ operational capabilities and commitment to maintaining security, highlighting that the forces had thwarted plans of elements seeking to destabilise the country.

He noted that the forces had been conducting effective actions in different regions to counter terrorism and prevent attacks on civilians and state institutions.

The interior minister emphasised that Pakistan’s fight against terrorism required continued national unity and support for the institutions

‘Coordinated’ attack in Bhag foiled

Earlier in the day, the Balochistan government issued a statement on the Bhag attack, saying that two policemen were among five people injured as law enforcers foiled a “coordinated” terrorist attack on a police station, bank and the assistant commissioner’s office.

Shahid Rind, the chief minister’s aide for political and media affairs, said in a post on X that about 40 terrorists attacked the three places using “heavy weapons, rocket launchers, machine guns, sniper rifles and hand grenades”.

Rind said the terrorists failed to take control of the Bhag police station or seize weapons from the facility.

He highlighted that the cops “bravely confronted the terrorists for nearly two hours”, inflicting heavy casualties and material loss to the attackers, who were “forced to retreat”. The CM’s aide noted that the strong protective wall of the police station played a crucial role in the defensive action.

Rind further said that the terrorists failed to loot cash from the “national bank”, while a special branch of the Bomb Disposal Unit defused an IED planted by the terrorists in the facility.

Two police personnel were injured by the terrorists’ firing, while three citizens were also hurt, Rind said, adding that medical aid was being provided to them all.

Following the terrorist attack, the people of Bhag expressed solidarity with police and lauded their bravery, he said, affirming that the people of Balochistan stood with police and security forces in the fight against terrorism.

“Bhag police proved that terrorists would not be allowed to challenge the writ of the state,” Rind asserted.

Surge in terrorism

The series of counterterrorism operations come amid a recent surge in terrorist activities in Balochistan.

On the night of Aug 31-Sept 1, Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) terrorists launched a coordinated attack on the Customs House, located at Ziarat Cross on the N-50 National Highway, in Pishin district.

While security forces responded effectively and killed 10 terrorists, two officers were among six martyred in the fire exchange, ISPR said.

Also on August 31, 11 terrorists belonging to Fitna al-Hindustan, who had blocked the N-40 Quetta-Taftan highway by establishing an illegal checkpoint for extortion in Chagai’s Nokcha area, were eliminated following an intense exchange of fire.

According to security officials, a convoy of “empty vehicles” from the Reko Diq copper and gold project had come under attack in the same area of Nokcha while it was travelling to Quetta from the project site.

The same day, it was reported that two terrorists had also been killed during an IBO in Washuk district.

Last month, the security situation remained most severe in Balochistan, where the number of terrorist attacks increased by seven per cent from 83 in July to 89 in August, according to a monthly assessment by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS).

World.title: Govt transfers ISI’s internal wing chief Maj Gen Faisal Naseer to Nacta
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The government, in a surprise move on Friday, transferred Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI) Director General (C) Major General Faisal Naseer and appointed him National Coordinator of the National Counter-Terrorism Authority (Nacta).

The DG (C) post is often mistakenly described as heading ISI’s counter-intelligence wing. The office actually heads the agency’s Internal Wing, which deals with domestic security and other matters and, because of the nature of the assignment, frequently engages with the country’s principal power centres.

Within the ISI, DG (C) is considered virtually the second most important position after that of the ISI director general.

Maj Gen Naseer’s transfer is being seen as particularly significant because it comes ahead of the upcoming promotions in the army. An officer from the Corps of Military Intelligence, he was considered a strong candidate for elevation to the rank of lieutenant general.

He served as DG (C) from 2022, shortly after his promotion to the rank of major general, and remained in the position through a politically turbulent period.

Although there have been exceptions over the years, a transfer to a non-military assignment may affect an officer’s career progression, hence the surprise among many observers of military affairs.

Nacta, established in 2009 and subsequently given statutory backing under the Nacta Act of 2013, was conceived as the country’s central civilian body for coordinating counter-terrorism and counter-extremism policies among federal and provincial agencies.

In practice, however, the authority has never fully evolved into the command and coordination body envisaged under the law and has largely remained a policy secretariat with limited capacity to enforce decisions across the country’s sprawling security and law enforcement apparatus.

The authority has also seen frequent changes at the top, with more than a dozen National Coordinators since its inception, most of them drawn from the police service.

Maj Gen Naseer’s appointment therefore marks a departure from the usual practice and could potentially signal an attempt to give greater weight to an institution that has long struggled to establish itself as the central coordinating mechanism for the fight against terrorism and violent extremism.

The government did not immediately explain the rationale for the change.

World.title: Govt reduces petrol price by Rs3.13, increases HSD by Rs3.74
World.content:
The government on Friday reduced the price of petrol by Rs3.13 per litre while increasing the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs3.74 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs345.87 per litre while HSD will cost Rs378.05 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will remain in effect from Sept 5 (Saturday) to Sept 7 (Monday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

On July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Hesson says Pakistan players used to 'chaos' after shake-up
World.content:
Interim Pakistan head coach Mike Hesson hopes his drastically revamped squad can come through some all too familiar “chaos” with a much-improved showing against England in next week’s third and final Test in Birmingham.

Pakistan suffered an innings and 103-run loss in the series opener at Headingley, before going down by 194 runs at Lord’s on Sunday as England took an unbeatable 2-0 lead in the three-match campaign.

The Pakistan Cricket Board responded to those defeats in dramatic fashion, taking the extraordinary step of sending seven players home, calling up another seven and replacing sacked Test coach Sarfaraz Ahmed with Hesson, already Pakistan’s white-ball boss.

Senior players Imam-ul-Haq and Salman Ali Agha — Pakistan’s captain at Headingley when Babar Azam was injured — were among those told to leave. Left-arm spin bowler Ali Usman, who claimed a five-wicket haul at Headingley, and seamer Khurram Shahzad were also sent home.

Of the seven replacements, only batsmen Saim Ayub and Abdullah Fazal have Test experience.

Hesson, however, feels the whole squad can now unite and give a better account of themselves when the third Test at Edgbaston starts on September 9.

The New Zealander had recently been in Japan preparing for the Asian Games and was only due to travel to the UK for the squad’s audience with King Charles, which took place on Wednesday.

“I was heading over to see the King and be part of a nice occasion. That got expedited,” Hesson told reporters at Edgbaston on Friday, as quoted by the BBC. “The last couple of days have been challenging for being in a hotel with some players coming, some players going and then the arrival of everyone.

“The guys are probably more used to a little bit of chaos than I am. There is no doubt they have been disappointed, incredibly disappointed. We have had to park that and go ‘righto, where to from here?’ They have been really good over the past couple of days.”

Hesson added: “I don’t think anyone wants this to happen in the middle of a series.

“From my perspective, it is about putting a balanced squad together, not only for this Test, so we actually have some variety in our attack,” he adds. “Pakistan is known for the pace, unusual actions, mystery spin — we haven’t really been able to present any of that.”

World.title: UN adopts major map reform to show true scale of continents
World.content:
The United Nations General Assembly voted on Friday for a resolution spearheaded by several African countries to adopt a map that makes their continent bigger while shrinking North America and Europe — aiming at “a more accurate representation” of world geography.

The resolution was backed by 164 countries while the United States voted against it and six other states abstained.

The new map — known as the Equal Earth cartographic projection — “offers a more accurate representation of the sizes of continental landmasses and to this end is a relevant option for improving the accuracy of the cartographic representation of the world,” the resolution says.

It urges member states to adopt the new map in place of the traditional Mercator projection, which was designed for maritime navigation by Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator in 1569.

The foreign minister of Togo, which drove the resolution, said maps “shape our understanding of the world.”

“They guide education, nourish the imagination, and influence collective perceptions. They are therefore never neutral, when they present a distorted image of our planet, they risk perpetuating inaccurate representation that are passed down through generation,” Robert Dussey said at the UN.

The Mercator projection focused on accurate depictions of the shapes and angles of land masses, but their relative sizes were often inaccurate — in part due to the challenge of rendering a three-dimensional globe onto a two-dimensional map.

It inflated northern regions and compressed equatorial ones, making Europe and North America appear much larger, while shrinking Africa and South America.

A group of cartographers launched the Equal Earth projection in 2018. It makes Africa, Latin America, South Asia and Oceania appear vastly larger.

“Equal Earth preserves the relative surface areas of continents and, as much as possible, shows their shapes as they appear on a globe,” one of the cartographers, Bojan Savric, told AFP in 2025.

The foreign ministry of France — which co-sponsored the resolution in support of the new map — announced Friday that it would abandon the Mercator projection.
